535322|2026-03.headline: Repco Home Finance posted record FY26 disbursements of Rs.4,148 Crores (+26% YoY) and cut GNPA to 2.55%, while AUM growth of 9.6% to Rs.15,880 Crores lagged disbursements.
535322|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly (Rs.1,186 Crores) and annual (Rs.4,148 Crores) disbursements, with Q4 PAT of Rs.129.11 Crores versus Rs.108.77 Crores in Q3. Gross NPA fell from 3.26% in December 2025 to 2.55% in March 2026, and Stage 2 assets declined to about 7% from about 9.5% a year earlier. Loan book growth remained well below disbursement growth because of run-off, prepayments and balance transfers out. Management guided to Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement and Rs.18,000 Crores AUM for FY27, and a 75% total FY26 dividend.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Tamil Nadu contributes about 60% of disbursements. Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh improved QoQ, and management expects non-TN states to contribute materially more from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Product and customer mix
segments.commentary: Home loans are 71% and non-housing loans 29% of the book, and salaried customers are 46% (Rs.7,410 Crores) against non-salaried 54% (Rs.8,470 Crores). Yields are 11.16% for HL, 13.44% for non-HL, 11.36% for salaried and 12.27% for non-salaried.

segments.name: New book (post-2022 loans)
segments.commentary: GNPA on the new book is about 1% and Stage 2 is about 3.9%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target of about Rs.5,000 Crores, with expected repayments and prepayments of about Rs.2,940 Crores and year-end AUM target of about Rs.18,000 Crores.
Management said Rs.25,000 Crores AUM is now targeted about two years out, implying FY29 versus the earlier FY28 aspiration.
Q1 FY27 disbursement plan is about Rs.1,000 Crores, with management aiming to keep quarterly disbursements above Rs.1,000 Crores.
Stage 2 assets expected to fall below 5% before end of FY27.
Spread target of about 3.2% to 3.25% for FY27, down from 3.34% previously reported.
NHB refinance of Rs.600 Crores sanctioned; expected to cut cost of funds by about 10 to 15 bps. Cost of funds expected to stay flat next quarter, and to rise if RBI raises repo.
CSR spend expected to return to about 2% to 3% of average profit, from 5% in FY26; exact figure to be given next call.
Dividend payout to be maintained at elevated levels per management, though the FY27 interim/final split and quantum were not specified.
capex_capacity: Network of 242 branches including SAT centres; nine offices opened in FY26.
Average disbursement per branch per month is Rs.1.5 Crores to Rs.2 Crores, with a model of one branch head and one branch sales manager per branch.
Approximately 180 to 185 branch sales managers; management is adding feet-on-street in non-TN branches and restructuring high-performance branches.
demand_pricing: Balance transfers out (BT Out) average about Rs.30 to Rs.35 Crores per month, mainly to public sector banks, while BT In averages about Rs.45 to Rs.50 Crores per month, mainly from HFCs for self-employed borrowers. Management says net BT In is positive.

FY26 principal run-off was about Rs.2,670 Crores, comprising about Rs.700 Crores scheduled repayment and about Rs.2,000 Crores of prepayments, pre-closures and BT Out (including Rs.400 Crores of BT Out, Rs.256 Crores partial prepayment and Rs.1,675 Crores full closure).
Management is following risk-based pricing and has cut rates case by case to retain customers. Benchmark rates were cut 10 bps on 1 July 2025 and 10 bps on 1 February 2026.
Competitive market: management says spread and growth are in tension and it will sacrifice some spread to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.25,000 Crores AUM by FY28 aspiration still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the original timeline. Management now targets about Rs.18,000 Crores by FY27 end and about Rs.25,000 Crores two years later, i.e. about one year behind. Inorganic buying is limited to Rs.25 to Rs.30 Crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AUM growth well below disbursement growth, and is the new book also running down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed vintage run-off, self-employed customers making bullet and part prepayments, and BT Out. An analyst's data point suggested about Rs.3,000 Crores of run-off on the post-FY22 book; management acknowledged part prepayments on the new book but said there were no major pre-closures there.

qa_highlights.question: Can per-branch productivity support Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement with current sales staff?
qa_highlights.answer: Average disbursement per branch is Rs.1.5 to Rs.2 Crores per month, which management says is achievable with one branch head and one sales manager plus processing support. It also acknowledged that adding salespeople is an option but is constrained by cost-to-income targets.

qa_highlights.question: Will Stage 2 fall below 5% and how?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to get Stage 2 below 5% by the end of FY27. Rs.300 Crores was rolled back in FY26 through a dedicated collection vertical, and a separate team now targets B0 to B1 flows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated dividend payout continue?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the higher payout is not a one-off and management wants to continue the trend. The FY27 interim/final split and quantum will be decided later.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the pricing and cost of funds trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell from 8.75% to 8.5% over the year, and the NHB refinance should cut it by 10 to 15 bps. Yield is about 11.9%, and spread is expected at about 3.2% to 3.25% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q-o-Q growth flat in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Karnataka e-Khata issue is fading, Andhra Pradesh had team realignment in Q4 with new leadership, and it expects growth from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. It expects a much larger non-TN contribution from Q1 or Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Persistent prepayments and BT Out keep AUM growth (9.6% in FY26) well below disbursement growth. FY27 AUM target of Rs.18,000 Crores requires about Rs.2,060 Crores net addition.
Spread compression: yield fell to 11.9% from 12.07% while management targets a 3.2% to 3.25% spread, and cost of funds may rise if RBI raises repo.
Limited cost-of-funds relief: NHB refinance is worth about 10 to 15 bps, and bank borrowings (about 85% of funding) are MCLR-linked with no reduction expected.
Stage 2 target below 5% by FY27 end, versus about 7% now, depends on roll-back execution.
Sales productivity: a Rs.5,000 Crores target needs about Rs.1.5 to Rs.2 Crores per branch per month, and non-TN states remain weak.

Profit affected by one-offs of about Rs.46 Crores in FY26 (Labour Code Rs.15 Crores, silver jubilee Rs.5 Crores, CSR uplift Rs.15 Crores, daily-balance interest method Rs.11.53 Crores), with CSR expected to fall back to 2% to 3%.
Quarterly disbursement run-rate of about Rs.1,000 Crores to be sustained in Q1 FY27 (management guidance).
535322|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and dividends, but cautious and sometimes evasive on AUM growth, pre-closures and spread, which management attributed to vintage run-off and competition. Several answers were vague on specifics (CSR, FY27 dividend split, sales headcount), and management promised follow-up on the next call.

535322|2026-06.headline: Repco Home Finance Q1 FY27: disbursements Rs.843 Cr (vs Rs.829 Cr), AUM Rs.15,990 Cr up 8.9% YoY; management flags spread compression of up to 10bps.
535322|2026-06.overview: Sanctions rose to Rs.938 Cr from Rs.907 Cr in FY26 and disbursements edged up to Rs.843 Cr from Rs.829 Cr, with management attributing the soft quarter to April-May transfers and promotions. Net profit rose to Rs.114 Cr from Rs.108 Cr and NII to Rs.216 Cr from Rs.207 Cr, while GNPA was Rs.427 Cr (2.7%) versus Rs.405 Cr (2.6%) in the prior quarter. Management guided to a more aggressive disbursement stance, accepting a possible 10-12bps spread decline to fund growth and curb BT-outs. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs.5,000 Cr disbursements, 13-14% AUM growth and a Rs.40 Cr NPA reduction.

IT transformation completed in two phases, including mobile apps and API integrations with Perfios, CERSAI and CIBIL to shorten sanction turnaround.
Operating model verticalised: separate vertical for recoveries and SARFAESI, a separate sales vertical, DSAs, DSTs and connectors added.
demand_pricing: Customer rates start at 8.75% with an average of about 10.5% on housing loans; management says pricing is risk-based on 16-17 parameters and PSU-bank rates are not viable at its cost of borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is customer lending rate high versus banks, and why is the company not diversifying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rate depends on cost of borrowing (about 8.3-8.35%) and risk profile, and PSU-rate lending is not viable. It has no current plan to diversify beyond housing finance, and an HFC licence limits it to housing and mortgage loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 disbursement affected by cheque issues, and is there a Q1 backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end disbursements of about Rs.35-40 Cr roll over each month as a normal cycle; June's figure carries the operational impact and any backlog will be made up in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are June and July run-rates back to normal, and is the Rs.1,200 Cr Q2 target credible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June was good, July was better and August is expected to exceed that, and the MD said he was confident of Rs.1,200 Cr, while declining to give exact figures citing price-sensitive policy.

qa_highlights.question: Have pricing or customer policies changed, and what is driving the higher runoff?
qa_highlights.answer: No major policy change; sourcing focus shifted and some rate concessions were given to retain customers. Higher BT-outs reflect competitors targeting the company's visibility from more aggressive marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality deterioration business as usual, and can recoveries outpace provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA uptick to transfers and promotions. Soft NPAs (April 2025-June 2026 slippages, about 1,000-1,100 cases, 40-45 per RVM) are targeted for at least 50% reduction, worth Rs.70-75 Cr, and chronic NPAs are being pursued via SARFAESI.

qa_highlights.question: How much spread compression and what does it do to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is 3.44% with cost of funds at 8.31%, and ROA around 2.9%. Spread may fall 10-12bps (maximum 10bps) next quarter, then stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company recognising interest and disbursement only on cheque encashment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said AUM and disbursement are booked only after encashment, and management said this has been the practice for three to four quarters.

535322|2026-09.headline: Repco Home Finance Q2 FY27: disbursements rose to ₹1,205 crore (from ₹1,069 crore), gross NPA fell to 2.4%, and FY27 profit guided to about ₹490 crore.

Gross NPA fell to ₹396 crore (2.4%) from ₹474 crore a year earlier, and stage 2 assets declined to ₹1,154 crore from ₹1,324 crore. AUM grew about 9.2% year on year to ₹16,425 crore. Management guided to a sharper growth push, with a sub-2% gross NPA target by year end and a softer spread outlook as cost of funds rises.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OPEX rise QoQ, and why is Q3 now expected above Q2 when past trend was otherwise?

Management attributes stronger 3Q to independent sales and credit channels with no overlap.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate-hike sensitivity, fixed vs floating mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Liabilities are almost fully floating; assets reprice quarterly with ~3-month lag. Cost of funds may rise 10-15 bps, to be passed on with about one-quarter lag. Spread to settle at ~3.25-3.3% after retaining borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress in the South, Karnataka or drought-affected areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported no stress in South or Karnataka; majority of branches in urban/peri-urban metro tier 1-2 areas; cheque bounce ratio stable.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp asset quality improvement and the outlook for NPA and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Verticalised recovery team, separate soft and hard NPA handling, property sale push. NPA reduced from ~₹425 crore in June to ₹397 crore; target below 2% by year end. Interim dividend ₹5/share; no payout ratio defined yet.

535693|2026-06.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
535693|2026-06.overview: Consolidated top line crossed Rs 110 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 20.24% YoY and 17.95% QoQ, driven by EPC activity. Consolidated EBITDA rose 13.08% YoY to Rs 25.15 crore, while PAT grew 9.57% YoY to Rs 16.48 crore. Management said Rs 429 crore of orders were booked in the quarter and the order book stands at about Rs 1,600 crore, with roughly 50% yet to start. Management also addressed cash conversion, pointing to Rs 165 crore of OCCPS repayments from June 2027 and arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.04% in Q4 FY26 (as stated on call)

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Consolidated EPC revenue Rs 104.47 crore (vs Rs 87.53 crore in the prior quarter as stated on call); consolidated PBT Rs 14.71 crore (vs Rs 11.43 crore QoQ).

segments.commentary: Consolidated real estate revenue Rs 6.33 crore, up about 65% YoY from Rs 3.82 crore; real estate PBT Rs 5.40 crore. Management cites 85-90% margins for this segment.

guidance_outlook: Management targets FY27 order book of about Rs 2,500 crore by year-end, against roughly Rs 1,600 crore currently.
Management expects a historic top line and bottom line in FY27 and said it will keep EPC growth at the rate of the last 2-3 years.
Management expects no margin compression for FY28-FY29 and says growth will come from higher order inflow.
Around 80% of the Rs 800 crore-plus order book to be executed over 18 months is expected to bill in the first year, per management.
New mixed-use shopping mall (Rs 500-700 crore valuation) to start construction by year-end; first phase rent yield from FY29-FY30, with three-phase rental target of Rs 50-60 crore annually.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028 once Section 43B deductions on past interest run off; FY27 effective rate 12-15%.
capex_capacity: Current order book about Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months.
Bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore; focus on railways, institutional buildings (universities, medical colleges), and flood and slope protection works.
Ramping up flood protection technical team by recruiting more engineers.
Balance sheet: bank guarantee limit Rs 100 crore and CC limit Rs 100 crore; soft surety bond limit about Rs 50 crore, enabling bids of up to Rs 1,000 crore more.

Land and assets: about 4 lakh sq ft of shopping mall area, industrial park on 100-200 acres, 30-35 bigha land parcel; land value Rs 100-200 crore and City Centre valuation Rs 600-700 crore (management estimate).
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order inflow of Rs 429 crore across railways, roads and highway maintenance; over Rs 300 crore booked in the last 75 days.

Major orders: Rs 140 crore road-over-bridge for Northern Central Railway; Rs 81.98 crore staff quarters for NF Railway; Rs 70.18 crore five-year O&M from MoRTH on a Mizoram NHAI corridor; Rs 25.78 crore Assam road maintenance from NHIDCL.
Management says it is selective on bids and avoids hyper-competitive volume work; about 50% of the order book is outside Northeast India.
Wayside Amenities (NHAI land leases, 30-year) bids pending; results expected next month.
Management states that cash-flow issues are concentrated in pre-2020 legacy projects now in arbitration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book for FY27 and FY28, and what is the bid pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book of Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months; bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore, focused on railways, institutional buildings and flood/slope protection.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash conversion improve given large receivables, WIP, retention and OCCPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no stuck-up money or slow-moving WIP on post-2020 projects; debtors about Rs 15-20 crore with 45-90 day billing cycles. Pre-2020 legacy projects in arbitration: over Rs 100 crore monetised in five years, about Rs 150 crore still pending, with Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years including bank guarantee releases. OCCPS of Rs 165 crore repayment starts June 2027 and runs to 2034; management plans to swap OCCPS with arbitration awards.

qa_highlights.question: Is real estate a core hedge or to be divested?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to divest; both segments to operate jointly. Mall development is planned to start by year-end with rental income of Rs 50-60 crore at full three-phase build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Assam floods on ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of works are outside Northeast and unaffected; some Upper Assam projects were affected, but emergency variation works offset this with no negative impact on billing or turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How is pan-India expansion being pursued and does it include light real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is selective, project-by-project; West Bengal is a strategic target. Asset-light real estate via NHAI Wayside Amenities bids is being pursued, with a large Assam bid awaiting results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 12-15% effective rate reflects Section 43B deductions on past interest; expected to move to 20-22% after 2028.

Real estate and mall project depends on compliances; construction start expected by end-FY27 and rental income only from FY29-FY30.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028, which will lower PAT growth versus the current 12-15% rate.

key_quotes: In fact, 50% of our current order book is yet to start.
There is no backlog and there is no slow-moving WIP as of date.

So, we are very much confident that in the subsequent quarters, the same momentum with the healthy bottom line will be continue and we keep, expect all the stakeholders support and we are very much sure that in 2026-2027, we will give a historic number from the top line and from the bottom-line point of view.
So, there is no stuck up of money, and currently, we are in a positive cash flow statement position.

535754|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR1 vs Dec quarter; down vs ~INR255 last year

segments.name: Sanghi Industries (acquired)
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Ambuja and ACC existing assets

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume guided at ~80 Mt, about 8% growth, versus industry growth of 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of INR250/t on a full-year average; cost peak of ~INR4,500/t in Q4, Q1 FY27 seen flattish, with savings accelerating over the remaining three quarters.
Minimum cost reduction of INR250/t in FY27 and another INR250/t in FY28 (INR500 cumulative); management says the earlier INR3,650/t target is not abandoned.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Recalibrating growth capex: shutting some grinding units in North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat and Maharashtra to move them closer to markets; a Bihar grinding unit planned; Dahej Line 2 as clinker-plus-cement example.
Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Industry price rise in March quarter was about INR10/bag, INR15-20 only in selected pockets; management says industry cannot pass on costs under relentless pricing pressure.
April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

Pricing power in a soft demand environment; April-May trend described as subdued.

Non-core working capital, MSA receivables from ACC, and negative ACC operating cash flow, to be resolved via ICD.
Reduced government incentives after GST rate cuts and changed accrual policy.

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; from INR4,447/t in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated cost base cited by analyst

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74% QoQ; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volumes -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Trade volumes grew 2% YoY; management calls it the highest-EBITDA cluster. Roughly 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; about 30% of volume mix.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Trade volumes sustained with healthy margins; about 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes deliberately reduced; blended cement push lifted margins. About 10% of volume mix.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Highest YoY degrowth as about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume were cut; about 10% of volume mix. Channel build-out expected to take one to two quarters.

segments.name: RE power and fly ash (other operating income)
segments.commentary: About 45 crore units of RE power sold in Q1 for roughly INR140 crore revenue (vs 24 crore units / ~INR70 crore in Q4); fly ash sales about INR15 crore in Q1 vs ~INR50 crore in Q4. Both are netted in operating cost per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 8%; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY. Trade share guided to remain above 75%.
Full-year FY27 net cost target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below (about INR250/t further reduction).

Identified cost levers worth INR130-150/t: about INR35/t lead distance cut (15 km), INR30/t from raw material logistics and fly ash sourcing, INR50/t from energy (heat rate, power units, 75 MW new RE), and INR10-15/t other headroom.
Q2 FY27 net cost guided to be slightly better than June-quarter levels, after absorbing potential geopolitical cost rise of about INR100/t.
Capex FY27 about INR6,500 crore; Q1 spend about INR1,500-1,600 crore. FY28 capex similar at INR6,000-7,000 crore on a run-rate basis.
Installed capacity to reach 119 Mtpa by end-FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt); 8-10 Mtpa of organic additions planned each year thereafter.
Long-term capacity utilisation target 70-75% on a value-focused basis; green power share to reach 60% by FY28 (48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis).
capex_capacity: Trial runs started at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion); Salai Banwa (UP, 2.4 Mt) started; Bhatinda (Punjab, 1.2 Mt) and Jodhpur (Penna, 2 Mt cement / 3 Mt clinker) commissioned or stabilising, with Jodhpur clinker supplying grinding units from Q2.
Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).
Maratha clinker line (4 Mt) now expected Q1 FY28; Mundra expected 18-24 months out (around 2029).
RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.
Three coal blocks in focus; first expected to be operational in about 30 months. AFR (alternative fuel) substitution at about 7%, targeted at 10-15% in FY27.
Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.
demand_pricing: Management says cement demand was stable across infrastructure, housing and construction; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY.
Q1 headwinds: diesel availability, packing material shortages and logistics disruption in West and East. Logistics lead distance fell from 269 km to 249 km YoY, yet freight per tonne was flat.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed the gap to Incoterm and channel-cost netting. Analyst comparison put Q1 NSP about INR100/t below UltraTech's reported NSP.
Blended cement share 85%; clinker factor down about 3% to 64%.
Q2 FY27 cost pressure expected from geopolitical escalation (West Asia, fuel).

qa_highlights.question: Is it fair to expect muted FY27 volume growth if the value-over-volume strategy holds, given Q1 volume loss and earlier ~80 Mt chase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; non-trade is a 'well calculated' reduction, with market share said to have held or improved only on trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will green power be consumed in-house, and what is the incremental benefit as captive use rises versus selling power?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by diesel shortages, packing material issues and logistics disruption. North trade +2% YoY, West grew in trade and non-trade, East sustained, South cut about 1 Mt of low or negative EBITDA volume, Central degrew on blended-cement shift. Capacity utilisation 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping plants temporarily closed and treating non-trade differently at acquired assets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

risks_watch: Whether July's 8% trade volume growth holds and whether non-trade volume decline (-21% YoY in Q1) stabilises, given guidance needs roughly 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months.
Geopolitical and fuel cost pressure in Q2 (about INR100/t potential rise) versus the INR130-150/t cost-lever pipeline and the INR4,250/t full-year target.
Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Reconciliation gap: management did not provide a breakdown of cement vs RMC vs power vs fly ash cost, and deferred several analyst requests (fly ash/power cumulative P&L, RMC margin drop to about 7%, fixed cost bridge) to offline follow-up.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.
Green power transition: grid connectivity for some cement plants expected in two to three quarters, and green power share target of 60% by FY28 depends on consumption rising from about 50% of sales.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why TMRW revenue growth slowed and expected trajectory
qa_highlights.answer: Management said primary sales grew 11% vs 35% base last year and secondary grew 16-17%. Expects TMRW to deliver 20%+ revenue growth for the year and lower annual losses; FY27 is significant, with profitability targeted in FY29 to FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Period-end cash and debt; whether FY27 is still an investment year
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone gross cash about INR1,000 crores vs roughly INR1,150-1,200 crores at start of year, with about INR500 crores expected by year-end. Losses to be lower on an annual basis in FY27 and lower again in FY28, with full profitability in FY29. TMRW has already raised INR500 crores for its own growth plan.

qa_highlights.question: Pantaloons LTL trajectory after Q4 and adjustment for Adhik Maas; demand read
qa_highlights.answer: April was weak, May significantly double-digit, June softer; quarter LTL about 4% vs 14% in Q4, which included an EOSS shift. Management targets at least high-single-digit LTL for the full year and described demand as steady, not strong.

qa_highlights.question: TCNS LTL slowdown to about 2% and outlook
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a disappointing quarter for organic performance, citing liquidation of old inventory over the past 12-15 months; margin was slightly better YoY. Store additions of 35-40 are expected, with LTL returning to high-single-digit to early double-digit in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Ethnic segment growth outlook for FY27 given weak H1 and TCNS drag
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the overall ethnic portfolio to grow 20%+ for FY27, with H2 significantly higher than H1. TCNS is expected to return to early double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Galeries Lafayette revenue run rate, losses, and additional store plans; TMRW store and profitability plan; Tasva economics
qa_highlights.answer: Galeries Lafayette revenue not disclosed; still operationally loss-making. The Collective plus Galeries Lafayette expected to break even at combined level in H2 FY27. Next store planned in Delhi in 2-3 years. Tasva needs INR400-500 crores revenue to turn profitable; plans 25-30 new stores on ~90 base and sees mid-teens LTL.

qa_highlights.question: Inflation, pricing, and margin outlook for Pantaloons and OWND
qa_highlights.answer: Input inflation about 4%+ in both businesses; about half passed on in pricing. Cost pressure expected mainly in Q2 and Q3, with gross margin impact in H2. No higher discounting expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27
qa_highlights.answer: Capex plus working capital about INR450 crores for FY27, with capex about INR300+ crores for new stores and renovations.

key_quotes: We are confident that this cash is enough for us to fund the businesses for next 2 years, with annual cash funding requirement of INR500 crores to INR550 crores.
So I would say overall, not a very good quarter for the business.

535789|2026-03.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
535789|2026-03.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.name: Residential mortgages (prime and affordable)
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market home loans (8.5% to 10% yield) to be sourced for sale to banks; affordable portion (10% to 13%) to be held on balance sheet. Management says mortgages drive growth in FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: Business loans and micro-LAP
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.name: CRE project loans
segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

segments.name: Gold loans and loans against securities
segments.commentary: Planned as the next secured products; gold needs a separate branch network, with wider product launches from FY28. About 240 branches are already sized for other products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements of about INR30,000 crore; Q1 FY27 disbursements to be at least 50% to 60% above Q4 FY26, then a 30% to 40% step-up on that base.

Marginal cost of funds to fall about 160 bps; cost of funds to decline 150 bps over three years; 270 bps total reduction tied to AA to AAA migration (120 to 150 bps on AA to AA+, and the rest on AA+ to AAA).
Portfolio mix target: 60% secured and 20% unsecured or semi-secured, with 80% retail; about 30% of incremental disbursements through co-lending or direct assignment.
Gearing capped at about 3.5x to 4x; liquidity held at the higher of 6 months of repayments or 10% to 15% of borrowings.
Target AUM of INR2 lakh crore and high-teen ROE (about 18%), with the timeline described as 'in no hurry'; FY27 and FY28 growth to be mainly mortgages.
capex_capacity: Branch network to grow fivefold to about 1,600 branches; workforce to rise to 20,000 people, with about 8,000 by end of FY26 per management.
A gold loan branch costs about INR20 lakh to set up and takes about 3 years to become fully productive and profitable; investment is not described as running into tens or hundreds of crore.
Technology spend (CRM upgrade and Salesforce deployment about 6 months ago) is expensed through the P&L, not capitalised; 37 AI use cases identified.
Targets: agent productivity up 30%, mortgage turnaround from 5 to 7 days to 2 to 3 days, loans per person per month from 0.6 to 2-plus.
demand_pricing: Management says productivity rose 2x between March and April 2026 following the shift to an asset-light model.
Disbursals of about INR72,000 crore planned for FY29 versus INR50,000 crore in CY17 and CY18 (as cited by management).
Competition: management says there are few AAA-rated NBFCs and that the market has room for new entrants; it cites AAA players (and 3 to 4 other AA+ players) disbursing around INR50,000 crore a year.
Management says insurance cross-sell reaches over 90% of borrowers.
Management says about 90% of borrowings are onshore; domestic bonds have appreciated about 100 bps since the IHC announcement, with international bonds about 250 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Ahuja (BlackRock): Will offshore rating agencies follow the onshore upgrades, and is the slow cost-of-funds decline due to non-call fixed-maturity debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects international agencies to follow the domestic upgrades. Bonds cannot be renegotiated and have 3 to 4 year maturities, so the cost decline comes with a lag; incremental borrowing at lower cost and bank renegotiation are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI Bank): How will the company build non-mortgage portfolios, who will run them, and how will costs be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has run secured and unsecured products at scale before, that tech and app-based lending help, and that people and tech investment will be made. Growth in FY27 and FY28 will be mainly mortgages, given no rush to hyper-grow.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): What share of growth comes from core versus new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 and FY28 disbursals are 80% existing products, falling over time; by FY30 the mix is targeted at 50% mortgage-backed and 50% other products.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash Singh (Emkay): How will competition from AAA NBFCs be handled, and is the FY30 ROA of about 8% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the FY30 ROA figure was an error and corrected it to 4.4%, with FY27 at 1.8%, FY28 at 3.7% and FY29 at 4.4%. It says the market is large enough and that mortgage front-loading and co-lending support productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Naintara Ghosh (Deutsche Bank): How much investment is needed for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is mainly branches and people rather than large capex; technology costs already incurred (CRM, Salesforce) run through the P&L, and product-level ROA can be shared on request.

qa_highlights.question: Vineet Sharma (Param Capital): What drives the NIM rise from 3.5% to 5.8% when cost of funds is not falling as fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NIM gain comes from the spread on sold-down loans (AUM less loan book rising from about INR30,000 crore to INR45,000 crore in FY28), and that equity adds liquidity without a P&L cost. Cost of funds shown is for on-balance-sheet borrowings only.

qa_highlights.question: Arun Antony (JM Financial): Is the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction for FY27 still achievable given the West Asia conflict and rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 270 bps, with 120 to 150 bps coming from AA to AA+ and the rest from AA+ to AAA, and said the company is operationally, financially and promoter-ready for AAA.

qa_highlights.question: AS Raju (individual investor): What is the outstanding write-off as of 31 March, and will recoveries be included in projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recoveries of about INR7,000 crore from amounts provided are built into the projections and described the provisions as credit costs, not write-offs. It said asset reconstruction company sales recover 70% to 80%.

risks_watch: Execution on FY27 disbursals (INR30,000 crore) and Q1 FY27 step-up; management's productivity claims rely on a 2x jump in one month.
Cost-of-funds path: 270 bps depends on AA to AAA migration; international agency ratings are still pending, and about 90% of borrowings are onshore.
Warrant balance of about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due within 18 months, plus IHC's rise to 43.5%.
Credit-cost and recovery assumptions: the legacy book had provisions, with recoveries of about INR7,000 crore assumed; the call did not give a detailed write-off schedule.
Cost-to-income falling from ~50% to ~26% while hiring and building new products, with a risk of cost overrun during the transition.
A FY30 ROA projection error was corrected on the call; the revised presentation should be checked for other inconsistencies.

It was evasive on some specifics, such as the write-off quantum, and it corrected the FY30 ROA figure during Q&A.

535789|2026-06.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.
535789|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the first quarter under IHC ownership, with PAT of INR243 crores after last quarter's balance-sheet markdowns. Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

financial_highlights.change: Following balance-sheet markdowns and provisions taken in the prior quarter; no YoY comparison stated
Stated as in line with guidance; no QoQ figure given

Described as standard in normal course of business
Down about 50 bps during the quarter
International rating upgraded from B+ to BB-

segments.commentary: About INR2,000 crores disbursed in Q1, the largest product by disbursement; micro LAP planned as a mainstay.

segments.name: Loans against securities / unsecured / credit-fund deal
segments.commentary: Loans against securities INR262 crores and unsecured about INR100 crores in Q1; one INR840 crore co-lending deal with an Asia-based credit fund (20% Sammaan, 80% fund).

guidance_outlook: Disbursements: INR10,000 crores in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crores in H2, total INR30,000 crores for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.
Cost of funds: 9.6% by September, 9.3% by end-FY27, and 7-8% range over the next 2-3 years; management said below 8% over three years.
Cost-to-income: about 50% in FY27, declining from H2 FY28, targeted at 30-35% by FY29.
Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27, rising to 270, with 800 branches targeted by end of FY28.
Five-year targets cited on the call: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%, as put out on May 20.
Inorganic growth to be considered from FY28; the bias for now is to build.
capex_capacity: Branch network to rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 23 master service centres across 20 states; management targets 800 branches by end of FY28.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, integrating a new Salesforce-based CRM and a new loan management system, plus a data lake.
Digital personal loans to launch on the app in H2 FY27; gold loans, two-wheeler loans and BNPL-type e-commerce tie-ups targeted by end-FY28.
53 AI use cases under implementation, with about 60% to be implemented in FY27; about 66% of identified use cases reportedly in motion.
Hiring: mid-level and ground-level offer-to-join cycle is 90-120 days; senior management hires expected to be announced towards the end of Q1/start of Q2.
demand_pricing: FY27 disbursement mix: about 75% mortgage-backed (two-thirds retail, one-third wholesale AUM with about 20% kept on balance sheet), 25% new products; about 90% secured and 10% unsecured in FY27, moving to 80:20 in FY28.

Securitisation and asset-light model: at least 30% of origination to be securitised or sold down, with 60-70% kept as a backup option; assets below 9.5% to be sold down via direct assignment, above 9.5% sliced between balance sheet and securitisation.
Asset yield universe cited from 8.5% (prime) to about 20% (unsecured); LAP 11-12% and affordable loans 12-13% also eligible for securitisation.
Fee income expected to rise, with direct assignment fee income kicking in around October 2026 with about a six-month lag.
97% of Q1 disbursements and 97% of AUM are secured.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Will lower cost of funds be passed on to customers for acquisition, or will spreads be retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rides on lower cost of funds plus asset-light model; sub-9.5% assets to be sold down via direct assignment and higher-yield assets kept or securitised, balancing fee and spread income.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): How much upfront opex and what is the cost-to-income path?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex will rise in absolute terms, offset by fee income with a lag of a quarter or two; cost-to-income around 50% this year, declining from H2 FY28, reaching 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Abhiram Iyer (Deutsche Bank): What is the asset-class breakup of the roughly INR3,000 crore per half target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 mix about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products; disbursement breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Agarwal (Bajaj Alternates): What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 90 bps saving on about INR50,000 crore borrowings (about INR450 crore annualised), targeting a further 70 bps; software procurement at 30-50% of earlier costs; and senior talent additions.

qa_highlights.question: Sanket (DAM Capital): What is IHC's larger vision beyond lending in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: Niharika (CapGrow): Are the five-year ROE, ROA and NIM targets achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident, citing rating upgrades, lower cost of funds, asset-light model and tech, with governance as the enabler.

qa_highlights.question: Nilesh Sharma (Monomer): What are disbursement targets for this and next financial year?

Recoveries and asset quality: management said recoveries will exceed internal projections and that no P&L pain is expected, but the Q1 PAT of INR243 crores relies on net recoveries of INR240 crores; watch recovery run-rate and ARC sale outcomes.

Governance and inorganic plans: statutory auditor change and internal audit co-sourcing partner selection were said to be closing this quarter; inorganic growth deferred to FY28.

537291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 4,316 million, but gross margin normalised to 56% from 63% and PAT fell about 8% to INR 384 million.
537291|2026-03.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported FY26 revenue of INR 4,316 million (+19% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 525 million (12% margin) and PAT of INR 384 million (9% margin). Gross margin fell to 56% from 63% in FY25 on richer product and market mix, and the tax rate rose to 11% from 5%. Growth was led by maize (volume +54%, value +78%), paddy (volume +25%, value +37%) and cotton Bt, while plant nutrition fell 18% on China export restrictions. Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% (calling 15% the base case) with slightly higher EBITDA and net margins, though guidance was qualified as conservative.

538268|2026-03.headline: Wonderla Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR135 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR43.8 crore at 32% margin, helped by Chennai ramp-up and a Labour Code provision reversal.
538268|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever Q4 by income, with revenue from operations up 40% YoY to INR135 crore and footfalls up 30% to 8.79 lakh, driven mainly by the newly opened Chennai park. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?

538562|2026-03.headline: Skipper Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY) and PAT rose 70% to INR75.6 crore; FY27 guided to 15% revenue and ~30% PAT growth.
538562|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: revenue INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY), EBITDA INR173.4 crore (+40.2%, margin 10.4% vs 9.6%) and PAT INR75.6 crore (+70%, margin 4.5%). FY26 revenue reached INR5,552.8 crore (+20%) with PAT of INR207.3 crore (+42%) and EBITDA margin of 10.3%. Order book closed at a record INR8,501.9 crore on record FY26 inflows of INR5,678 crore, but management flagged a temporary slowdown in domestic bidding and export disruption from the Middle East conflict, and guided FY27 conservatively at 15% revenue growth. Trade receivables rose sharply to INR1,485 crore, which management attributed mainly to a INR260 crore collection slipping into April and higher domestic billing.

segments.name: Engineering (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,248 crore, up over 33% YoY; FY26 revenue INR4,359 crore, up 24% YoY on transmission infrastructure demand.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue crossed INR500 crore (about INR507 crore) as a record; volumes grew about 40% while value growth was lower due to lower commodity prices. Margin still low single digit.

segments.name: Infra / non-T&D
segments.commentary: Management said non-T&D is about 14% of the order book, mainly O&M for a BSNL project; infra revenue is largely T&D-driven. Order book has fallen from about INR2,000 crore to about INR1,000 crore over 6-7 quarters, per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15% revenue growth (conservative, on an elevated base) and about 30% bottom-line growth, which management said is backed by the existing order book rather than new orders.
No explicit FY27 EBITDA margin number; management expects some margin improvement over FY26 but called it a challenging year with higher costs. Long-term aspiration is 12% EBITDA margin.
Management expects a return to 20-25% growth from FY28 as exports reopen and domestic bidding recovers; order awarding expected to approach FY25 levels from FY27.
FY27 capex guided at about INR250 crore, similar to prior years.
Export order book targeted to rise to 25% and eventually 50% of the order book (currently about 10%).
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes is due for commissioning by June 2026 (spillover from March), taking capacity to 450,000 tpa; utilisation above 85%.
Further 75,000 tpa planned in each of FY27 and FY28, targeting 600,000 tpa by FY28.
Management expects significant use of the new 75,000 tpa from Q3 FY27; full utilisation takes a couple of quarters. Expansion is expected to add about INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue annually.
Test Bed 2 commissioned, giving dual test beds at one location; a 293-tonne tower test set a record and a 350-tonne test is planned next month.
Growing substation business: about 4 high-voltage substation projects currently being executed.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,501.9 crore (90% domestic, 10% export); FY26 inflows INR5,678 crore; Q4 inflow INR1,029 crore.
Bidding pipeline over INR33,000 crore, about 60-65% domestic and balance export; historical order conversion of 20-25%.

FY26 domestic bidding was well below FY25 because of ROW, forest clearance and transformer/HVDC equipment constraints; several projects (e.g., Krishnagiri REZ Ph-1, Vizag-Kakinada-Tuticorin, 800 kV Barmer HVDC) slipped into FY27. Management said bidding rebounded in April.

Export pressure: Middle East disruption and higher sea freight are slowing decisions in export markets; management said freight is largely passed through via FOB/CIF renegotiation and export is about 10% of the order book.
Pricing: mix of variable- and firm-price contracts; management said firm-price contracts carry buffers for commodity inflation. Raw materials are 100% indigenous.

Market share: Power Grid holds about 50% of TBCB bids and is over 90% of the domestic order book; private developers under 10%. Skipper claims about 50% of transmission-line capex as addressable (about INR50,000 crore on a INR1 lakh crore annual base).

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables almost double to INR1,485 crore despite 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a INR260 crore receipt due in late March came in on 1-2 April, and domestic Q4 revenue rose about 45% YoY with longer domestic realisation cycles plus GST; INR600-700 crore was already realised in April. Management said none of the debtors are sticky.

qa_highlights.question: What conversion ratio applies to the INR33,000 crore pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically 20-25%; management hopes to maintain that but declined to give an inflow number.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance only 15% if order book is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Export execution is uncertain given geopolitics and export orders are unlikely to execute this year; management called 15% conservative on an elevated base, with effort to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact guidance; management expects to improve on FY26's about 50 bps gain, with long-term aim of 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company move more capacity to domestic and maintain 20% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic bidding was weak in FY26 and it is pursuing domestic opportunities, but kept guidance conservative; 20-25% growth expected from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for private-developer HVDC projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Private players are under 10% of the order book; management is in active talks with Tata Power, Adani and Resonia and says it is fully qualified for HVDC, currently executing a couple of HVDC projects.

qa_highlights.question: Are polymer non-Eastern market gains on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes grew about 40%, and presence has expanded outside the East, but the company is still small versus national players and remains focused on the Eastern region.

qa_highlights.question: Is the substation business margin-dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation projects carry margins similar to the Engineering business on a project basis, though infra EPC is lower margin in general.

risks_watch: Receivables: confirm the INR260 crore April collection and the remaining receivables in the Q1 FY27 numbers.
Execution: right-of-way and forest clearance delays and transformer/HVDC equipment shortages could push project timelines.
Exports: Middle East disruption and sea freight costs may slow order decisions; export share target of 25% depends on this.
Capacity ramp: 75,000 tpa due by June 2026 and utilisation from Q3 FY27; slippage already happened once.
Margins: 30% PAT growth guidance relies on firm-price buffers absorbing commodity inflation; no EBITDA margin number was given.
Bidding: CEA's FY27 tender timing and the INR90,000-1,00,000 crore PGCIL bid pipeline must actually come through.

rows.why: Management said bidding rebounded in April and historical conversion is 20-25% of a INR33,000 crore pipeline, which implies roughly INR6,600-8,250 crore of potential bids, but no inflow target was given and FY26 inflows were INR5,678 crore.

538562|2026-06.headline: Skipper Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.5% to a record INR1,310 crore, EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore, margin 10.7%; FY27 guided at 15% growth.
538562|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 4.5% YoY to a record INR1,310 crore, with EBITDA up 10% to INR140 crore and margin expanding 60 bps to 10.7%. PAT rose 26% to INR56.5 crore, helped by lower finance costs and operating leverage; management said the INR433.5 crore preferential equity raise came in late July/early August and did not benefit Q1. Order book closed at a record above INR9,200 crore and Q1 inflows were about INR1,674 crore (call also cites INR1,600 crore). Management reiterated 15% FY27 revenue growth and said the year is H2-weighted, with Engineering (export-heavy) soft in Q1.

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR1,674 crore (INR1,600 crore cited later)

segments.name: Engineering (incl. export)
segments.commentary: Soft in Q1 on low export and domestic order intake in FY26 and customers deferring shipments due to high freight costs; management called it temporary. Export order inflow guided up more than 50% YoY, about INR1,100 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Polymer
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue muted versus last year's above INR500 crore run-rate due to commodity price volatility and trade destocking; management guides about 20% top-line growth for FY27 with some margin improvement.

segments.name: Infra (EPC services)
segments.commentary: Strong growth in Q1 and past two quarters; revenue of about INR250 crore over two quarters cited. Management expects higher growth in this segment for FY27. Order book of about INR1,800 crore is infra, roughly 25% of order inflow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%, reiterated despite Q1 growth of about 5%; management expects H2 weighting.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,000 crore-plus, implying closing order book of INR10,000 crore-plus; about INR1,100 crore from exports.
Expects about INR5,000 crore of the INR9,200 crore order book to execute in FY27; orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.
FY27 finance cost expected at 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue after the fundraise.
Long-term aspirational EBITDA margin 12%; export share of order inflow targeted at 50% long term (about 15% in FY27, 20-25% next year per management).
Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes expected to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (a few months' deferment), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa.
Indian transmission bids expected at INR90,000-100,000 crore in FY27 vs INR50,000-60,000 crore TBCB bidding in FY26.
capex_capacity: 75,000 tonne capacity expansion to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (slight delay), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa; bulk of this capacity is export-focused.
Fundraise of INR433.5 crore via preferential equity; entire proceeds used for debt repayment per management.
Subsidiaries established in Brazil and UAE; US entity expected to become operational shortly.
Two 765 kV projects secured in Maharashtra from a reputed developer in Q1.
Legacy low-margin contracts now under 5% of order book, largely executing out this year.
demand_pricing: Steel spiked in Q1 but normalised to pre-February levels by May; aluminium also eased. Management said firm-price contracts carry buffers, variable-price contracts adjust monthly, and inventory build-up and partial hedging are used.

Export inflow hit by tariffs and Middle East geopolitics last year; management says export ordering has rebounded, with advanced talks in the US, Australia, and other developed markets; Europe slower pending approvals.
Export shipments being deferred by customers due to elevated shipping costs.
Order book by segment: about 75% T&D-related infra/EPC services versus 25% of total order book; Q1 inflow almost entirely T&D.
Biggest challenge cited: quality technical manpower; company takes about 200-250 graduate trainees annually.

qa_highlights.question: Is ordering picking up versus FY26, and what is the outlook for the Indian transmission market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ordering has picked up, bids are being finalised, and inflows should translate from Q2. It expects INR90,000-1,00,000 crore of Indian transmission bids in FY27 and said about 40% of the INR9 lakh crore pipeline has been bid so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the finance cost decline due to the fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Fundraise funds arrived late July or early August, so Q1 had no benefit; the decline came from working capital management and operating leverage. FY27 finance cost guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is export revenue lost or delayed, and which segment drives 15% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export ordering has not stopped and export order inflow should rise more than 50% YoY. The 15% growth is expected from all three segments, with Infra growing fastest; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally slow due to monsoon, West Bengal elections, and freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR5,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, with short-term orders adding to this. Orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Polymer revenue muted and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to commodity price volatility and trade destocking. It expects about 20% Polymer top-line growth in FY27 with margin improvement, and says growth will come from both volume and value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited legacy low-margin contracts rolling off, better new-contract quality, operating leverage, and commodity mitigation through firm/variable price mix, inventory and hedging. It called the expansion structural and aimed toward 12% long-term margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does the delay in capacity expansion affect the 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said commissioning is deferred only by a few months to end of Q2, with no impact on the 15% target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Engineering soften while Infra jumped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Engineering is affected by weak FY26 export and domestic order intake plus shipment deferrals due to high freight costs; it called this temporary. Infra growth is from TBCB transmission EPC services, with no change in scope of work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 order inflow target, and what is the export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR7,000 crore-plus of FY27 order inflow, with about INR1,100 crore from exports (about 15% of inflow).

risks_watch: Export execution: customers deferring shipments on high freight costs; export order inflow guided up more than 50% YoY (about INR1,100 crore) and orders from US, Australia and Europe still need approvals or advanced talks to convert.

Q2 inflow conversion: management said bids being finalised and inflows should translate from Q2; check whether Q2 order inflow tracks toward the INR7,000 crore-plus FY27 target (INR1,600-1,674 crore in Q1).
Revenue guidance back-end loaded: Q1 grew about 4.5% against 15% FY27 guidance; Q1 and Q2 seasonally slow; capacity commissioning of 75,000 tonnes now slipping to end Q2 FY27.

Commodity exposure: steel spiked in Q1 then normalised by May; margin sustainability depends on firm/variable price mix, inventory build and partial hedging; watch whether 10.7% margin holds in Q2-Q3.
Polymer volume: Q1 revenue muted versus above INR500 crore run-rate on destocking; 20% FY27 growth guidance needs recovery.
Finance cost: FY27 guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue after INR433.5 crore fundraise; Q1 had no benefit as funds arrived late July or early August. Track debt repayment and actual cost.

So overall for the year, we still maintain our 15% guidance. We are quite confident we will achieve that.
So I would say that these are temporary in nature. Long-term, the outlook is very, very positive.
I believe that this year, our finance cost should be somewhere between 3.2% to 3.5% for the whole year after this fundraise.

rows.why: Export order inflow guided to about INR1,100 crore (over 50% jump), with advanced talks in US, Australia and other developed markets, though Europe is slower pending approvals and export shipments are being deferred on freight costs.

rows.why: Proceeds are fully earmarked for debt repayment and guided finance cost of 3.2%-3.5% of revenue, down from 4.2% a year ago, though Q1 had no benefit since funds arrived late July or early August.

538562|2026-09.headline: Skipper Q2 FY27 revenue hit record INR1,384 crores (+10% YoY) and PAT rose 56% to INR57.5 crores, while management still targets 15% FY27 revenue growth.
538562|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record second-quarter revenue of INR1,384 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA of INR145 crores (+11%, 10.5% margin) and PAT of INR57.5 crores (+56%, 4.2% margin). Q2 order inflow was a record INR2,111 crores (+70% YoY), with export inflow of INR1,055 crores, and the order book stood at INR10,066 crores. Export shipments fell 46% YoY to about INR106 crores because customers are deferring shipments amid high freight rates. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 15% (at worst 13-14%), order inflow guidance of INR7,500 crores and export inflow guidance of INR1,500 crores.

segments.name: Infrastructure (EPC/projects)
segments.commentary: Management said Infra is the main driver of H1 revenue growth and will lead H2 growth; it carries lower EBITDA margins than Engineering, which analysts flagged as a margin-mix question.

segments.name: Engineering products
segments.commentary: Revenue growth was muted due to weak order inflows last year and export shipment deferrals. Management expects Engineering to grow in H2 and to even out across segments once new export orders execute next year.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Middle East now under 18% of export order book; North America about 44% and Australia about 18-19%, so developed markets are over 60%. Q2 export revenue fell 46% YoY to about INR106 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 15% maintained; management says at worst 13-14% given shipment deferrals.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,500 crores maintained; export order inflow target of INR1,500 crores maintained, with about INR1,000-1,100 crores already secured.
Employee cost expected at about 5.5% of revenue in Q3 FY27, after Q2 included Q1 arrears.
Operating cash flow expected to be at least 75% of total cash flow this year.
Net working capital days to stay in a 90-100 day range; long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 12%, with 10-11% described as the interim range.
H1 margin expansion of about 20-30 bps; management says margin expansion may be lower than planned but margins will not decline.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 75,000 MTPA (Phase 2, 375,000 to 450,000 MTPA) is on track for commissioning in H2 FY27, possibly end of Q3 or early Q4.
Longer-term roadmap of 600,000 MTPA by FY29; the next phase is likely greenfield and requires new land, with a location targeted for identification within the quarter.
Annual capex has been about INR250-300 crores, and the current expansion costs about the same; land cost may be added for greenfield projects.
Capacity utilisation was about 80% in Q2 on 375,000 MTPA; management says 90% is achievable but export deferrals are holding it back.
Preferential equity raise of about INR433.5 crores; CRISIL rating upgraded to A+/stable.
demand_pricing: Bidding pipeline above INR35,000 crores; management expects at least INR1 lakh crore of annual domestic transmission bidding through 2032-33.
Export shipments are being deferred by customers because freight rates are high; management believes freight has peaked.
Most new orders are fixed-price; management says firm-price orders carry a pricing buffer and higher down payments, so margin risk is low.
Export orders are mostly FOB; less than 25-30% of the export order book is CIF, so freight exposure is limited.
Management cites AI data-centre power transmission demand in the US, and a small acquisition in South India of about INR15-16 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% FY27 revenue growth target still achievable given H1 growth of about 7%, which implies about 21.6% in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is largely in line with 15%, and at worst the miss would be 1-2 points because of shipment deferrals; Q1 grew about 4-5% and Q2 about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the export order book is CIF and exposed to freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said less than 25-30% of the export order book is CIF, and the company has no risk from further freight escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the employee cost run-rate for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 was inflated by Q1 arrears paid with Q2 salaries; management expects Q3 employee cost at about 5.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual capex is INR250-300 crores; the current expansion costs about the same. Operating cash flow is expected to cover at least 75% of total cash flow, and debt-to-equity is 0.38x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the phasing and land status for the next capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 (to 450,000 MTPA) lands in H2 FY27; the greenfield site is being identified, with Phase 1 starting by end FY28 and full operation by FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital days were cut from about 200 to about 90 over 4-5 years; management expects 90-100 days to be stable and says export and domestic working capital are comparable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order inflow guidance achievable through exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept INR7,500 crores total and INR1,500 crores export inflow guidance, citing uncertain export order finalisation timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins hold at 10-11% in the interim?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; cost pressure from fuel and commodities may limit expansion, but margins will not drop.

risks_watch: Export shipment deferrals tied to high freight rates and Middle East conflict; Middle East exposure is still about 18% of export order book.
H2 revenue must grow about 21.6% to reach 15% for FY27; management now says the figure could be 13-14%.
Input cost inflation (fuel, commodities) is limiting margin expansion relative to plan.
Greenfield expansion needs a site and land acquisition, which adds cost and timing risk beyond Phase 2 commissioning.
Export order finalisation timelines are uncertain, which affects whether INR1,500 crores export inflow is achieved.
Infra-led revenue growth carries lower segment margins; monitor mix in Q3 and Q4.

538567|2026-03.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
538567|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. FY26 lubricant volume grew 10.5% to 1,68,000 KL, and consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crore for the first time. Margin pressure is building from the Middle East crisis and rupee depreciation, with crude moving from about USD 65-70 in February to USD 90-120 in March onward. Management is prioritising supply security and per-litre price pass-through, and is holding its 12-14% EBITDA margin band as the target. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

qa_highlights.question: What strategic levers are prioritised for FY27 in lubricants, OEM partnerships and EV-ready fluids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing segment-wise focus under 'Unlock 2.0' (accelerate, premiumise, transform), with digital initiatives, mechanic outreach and EV fluids for more than 30 OEMs. It aims to grow margins through premium products.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation and risk framework applies to dividends, R&D, hedging and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global R&D is funded by Gulf globally, so no direct P&L hit in India. Payout was lifted from 30-40% three to four years ago to c.72% for FY26, as cash builds and M&A and Tirex funding are still ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Chennai and Silvassa expansions on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Chennai is expected by Q3 and Silvassa by Q4 FY27; civil work at Silvassa is progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Are base oil availability and price rises hitting margins in Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold the 12-14% margin band and has cost levers. Supply has held so far, but a prolonged crisis could squeeze refiner supply chains. Prices are being raised repeatedly.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume driven by channel stocking or sustainable demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit growth ran through the year, with March-end boosted by supply-security buying from OEMs and distributors. Demand remains good into April-May.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume will be low and timing depends on which data centres are targeted; no revenue timing given.

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.

Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.

538666|2026-09.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR1,052 crore and PAT 23% to INR92 crore, despite a 5.1% volume decline.

Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products

segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.
