financial_highlights.change: about 20% EBITDA contribution per management; potential about INR100 crore, down about INR20 crore due to stoppages

segments.name: Spinning (cotton and blended yarn)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation at 99% in Q2 per management; exports about 52% of revenue. Demand from China and Bangladesh described as robust, with Bangladesh at about 45,000-50,000 tons and China buying about 60,000 tons.

segments.name: Fabric and garment entities (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Not yet merged; management expects merger within a couple of months. Combined H1 EBITDA ballparked at about INR80 crore, with output below potential due to restructuring stoppages.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 margins expected to stay close to H1 levels on the existing capacity; management declined to give a specific figure (19%, 18% or 21%).
Spreads guided at INR130-145/kg for the next three to four months; management said deviation of plus or minus 2% is possible.
Odisha 150,000-spindle project: commercial production in 30-40 days; FY27 contribution INR150-200 crore; FY28 revenue INR1,200-1,300 crore.
Odisha margins guided at least 4-5% (possibly 6%) above current company margins once operational; management said EBITDA positive from day one.
Peak long-term debt by March 2027 about INR700-750 crore; working capital below INR200 crore.
FY28: management reiterated at least 15% EBITDA margin, with upside possible but not guaranteed.
capex_capacity: Odisha Greenfield: 150,000 spindles, INR1,000 crore investment; building construction almost complete; full machinery package ordered and arriving in stages.
Commissioning of initial machinery expected in coming months; management said the whole project should finish by March 2027.
Solar power project commissioned; expected to cut annual power costs by about 15%.

Odisha incentives: 30% capital subsidy (about INR200-220 crore over 5 years), power at INR4/unit for 10 years, employment subsidy of INR7,000-8,000 per worker per month for 5 years, plus land-price rebate after 1,000 jobs.

Phase 2: land for another 300,000 spindles in Odisha; brownfield phase expected to take 2-3 months less than the Greenfield timeline; management said a second-phase trigger is expected in roughly 6-8 months, subject to debt levels.
Garment expansion plans to be announced possibly in H2 of next year.
demand_pricing: Management said yarn demand has risen for two to three quarters; visibility runs to about 10 March 2027, with demand the same or better.
Sales are typically on 80-90 day windows and about 120-day LC-backed credit terms.

Cotton prices fell from about INR70,000/candy to about INR65,500/candy; imported cotton landed at about INR67,000/candy per management. Blended cotton cost about INR150-160/kg (up from INR150 in Q1 per management).

Management expects Indian cotton prices to ease after Diwali, while the Indian yarn peak season after Diwali supports demand. Import duty waiver expected to be extended to December 2026 (per management, not yet notified).
Competition: management said new spindle announcements have been limited; consolidation and compliance costs are restricting smaller players.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin rise to 19.8% from 10.4%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better cotton and blended yarn demand over two to three quarters, operational efficiency gains from cost work over two to three years, and stable cotton prices over the past year; it expects similar conditions in the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Odisha project on track for Q3 FY27 commencement?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction is nearly complete and erection is underway; commercial production is expected in 30-40 days, with completion targeted by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 contribution and FY28 revenue from Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided INR150-200 crore in FY27 and INR1,200-1,300 crore in FY28; margins at Odisha expected to be 4-6% above current company margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are current spreads and how are inventory and cotton costs managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads are similar to the past six months; Q2 about INR141/kg versus INR133/kg in Q1; expected INR130-145/kg for three to four months. The company holds some cotton stock, sources from about 10 countries, and keeps about 3 months of order book cover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise to INR473.5 crore from INR396.2 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to higher billing and sales, LC-backed credit terms of about 120 days, and said receivable days are unchanged at about 58 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY28 margins and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated at least 15% EBITDA margin for FY28 with upside not guaranteed; peak long-term debt about INR700-750 crore by March 2027 and working capital below INR200 crore.

Receivables and LC-backed credit terms (about 120 days) and rising working capital.

Depreciation run-rate guidance changed after a method change (about INR7-8 crore impact).

539254|2026-03.headline: AESL FY26 capitalisation of about INR15,300 crores; FY27 capex guided at INR21,000-22,000 crores and capitalisation at INR21,000-22,000 crores.
539254|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a year of heavy commissioning, led by the Mumbai HVDC project (INR7,000 crores, commissioned 15 March 2026) and 82.29 lakh smart meters installed in the year against a 70 lakh target. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR21,000-22,000 crores (transmission about INR15,500 crores) and FY28 to about INR22,000-25,000 crores, with capitalisation of INR21,000-22,000 crores in FY27 and about INR13,000 crores in FY28. Credit ratings were described as improved to AAA+/AAA for most assets, with interest costs falling, and net leverage is to be held at 4.5x-4.7x. Management declined to give formal EBITDA guidance but said transmission EBITDA could reach about 3x current levels over 36-40 months and that FY27 consolidated EBITDA could be about INR11,500 crores versus INR8,726 crores in FY26 (as stated by the CEO).

539254|2026-06.headline: AESL Q1 FY27: Energy Solutions platform delivered about INR 570 crore EBIT on 3,325 MU long-term sales; management frames AESL as a full-scale utility.
539254|2026-06.overview: Management said AESL has moved to a full-scale utility with four operating businesses (transmission, distribution, smart metering, Energy Solutions) and expects consistent quarter-on-quarter reporting. Quarterly capex was close to INR 3,500 crore. Energy Solutions is the new focus: about 5 GW of take-or-pay supply and 3,500 MWh of storage tied up, with long-term offtake being built out. Management said the IntelliSmart acquisition is pending CCI approval. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of Energy Solutions margins, which management tied to whether purchase positions are back-to-back with sales.

segments.commentary: Described as growing at a stable pace; no segment figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected in INR900-1,000 crores; FY28 growth of 15-20% over FY27 cited, with the INR1,000 crores target for FY28 reiterated.
FY27 profitability expected around 6%, improving by 0.75-1% in FY28; a separate remark targets 7% by FY28 with EBITDA margin up another 2-2.5%.
Management expects raw-material cost pressure to normalise by Q3 or Q4 FY27; textile expected to turn good by Q3 FY27.
Near-term priority: neutralise the Q1 cost increase over the next two to three quarters and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.
Long-run revenue mix: textile 8-10%, FMCG 90-92%.
capex_capacity: Roorkee soap line commissioned in Q1 FY27 adds ~1,700 MT per month; aggregate FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity is 20,840 TPM (from 19,640 TPM at Q4 FY26).
Utilisation is currently ~50-55%; management expects another 25-30% utilisation gain by FY28.
Little further capacity addition expected over the next one to one-and-a-half years; only balancing capex is planned.
Bhilwara spices and savories plant runs one shift; second shift is free for expansion.
Management says existing capacity is enough to reach the INR1,000 crores FY28 revenue target without new capex.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to newly acquired units and new soap and FMCG capacity added in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, with customer base added during the quarter.
Business is B2B only; no B2C revenue. Over 200 customers, with quarterly planning forecasts and firm monthly orders.
Textile could not pass on dye, chemical and fuel cost increases in Q1; PP packaging prices spiked with geopolitical tension.
Spice margins described as lower and savory margins as higher.
Management expects revenue growth to come mainly from food and soap segments over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: How did raw-material and crude-linked costs behave in the quarter and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dyes, chemicals, consumables, boiler fuel and LABSA rose; PP packaging spiked. Textile prices could not be raised in Q1; management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR900-1,000 crores, FY28 growth 15-20%; FY27 profitability about 6%, rising 0.75-1% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raised funds went to Roorkee, and is further fundraising planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Roorkee capacity was funded from the subsidiary's retained earnings. INR98.65 crores raised was used for Bhilwara food and Guwahati soap/noodle/cosmetics facilities, not for Sunrakshakk Agro acquisition, which predated the raise. No further fundraising is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Will textile continue or be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger plans; textile is expected to improve by Q3 FY27 after a weak Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the next two to three quarter milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Offset the Q1 cost increase and raise utilisation of recently added capacity over three to four quarters.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 10.19% QoQ; recovery depends on input costs normalising by Q3 or Q4 FY27, which management itself flagged as uncertain given renewed pressure in Q2.
Utilisation of 50-55% versus the FY28 target rests on volume ramp; the INR1,000 crore target relies on existing capacity alone.
Textile profitability is weak; management expects a turnaround by Q3 FY27 but has not quantified it.
Working capital is described as balanced but management gave no specific target or days figure.
Some inconsistencies in the call: the FY28 margin guidance was given as +0.75-1% and, separately, as a 7% target with +2-2.5% EBITDA margin; the FMCG share was quoted as 90.60% and 90-91%.
539300|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and capacity, with a clear focus on profitability recovery. Answers were often vague or repetitive on cost and margin specifics, and the management struggled with several individual investor questions on audibility and wording.
key_quotes: Q1 FY'27 was our strongest quarter to date.
We believe that by Q3 or Q4 things will get normalized because Q2 we are seeing the impact of this situation again.
So, this year we will be closing somewhere between INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores mark.
So whatever capacities we had increased till now, that will give us a revenue of INR1,000 crores by FY28.
So as of now, we don't have any plan for additional fundraising.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 10.19% in Q4 FY26 on crude-linked dye, chemical, fuel and PP costs, and management expects normalisation by Q3 or Q4 FY27 with FY27 profitability around 6% and +0.75-1% in FY28, though renewed Q2 pressure is flagged as unresolved.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 1,700 MT/month Roorkee soap line is commissioned, lifting aggregate FMCG capacity to 20,840 TPM from 19,640 (about 8.7% added), but no further capacity is planned for the next 1-1.5 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets a 25-30% utilisation gain from about 52.5% by FY28, with growth coming mainly from food and soap segments, and revenue grew 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores with 200+ B2B customers.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 50-55% (about 52.5%), management says existing capacity can reach the INR1,000 crore FY28 target, and only balancing capex is planned, so a new capex announcement is not expected in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR900-1,000 crores needs roughly 3.3-3.6x the Q1 run-rate of INR276 crores over the remaining quarters, and margin recovery is unquantified, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue of INR276 crores implies a steep ramp to hit INR900-1,000 crores, EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 10.19%, and management itself flagged renewed Q2 cost pressure and an unquantified textile turnaround.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was discussed beyond the commissioned soap line.

rows.label: Textile price pass-through
rows.why: Textile could not pass on dye, chemical and fuel cost increases in Q1, and management expects textile to turn good by Q3 FY27 without quantifying it.

rows.label: No further fundraising
rows.why: Management said no further fundraising is planned, with Roorkee funded from subsidiary retained earnings and INR98.65 crores raised used for Bhilwara and Guwahati facilities.

rows.label: FMCG revenue mix shift
rows.why: FMCG and intermediates rose to about 90.60% of revenue from about 83% in FY26, with long-run textile guided at 8-10% of revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, capacity and the FY28 INR1,000 crore target, but cautious and vague on cost normalisation and textile recovery; analysts pushed on margin compression and the FY27 revenue ramp, and management struggled with some audibility and wording questions.

539301|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.
539301|2026-03.overview: Arvind SmartSpaces reported record FY26 bookings of INR1,550 crore, up 22% YoY, with Q4 bookings crossing INR600 crore for the first time. Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR163 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Contributed INR485 crore of FY26 bookings, about 31% of total. Arvind Skycrest in Bannerghatta sold 164 units worth INR262 crore (about 53% of inventory) within a week of launch.

segments.name: Vadodara
segments.commentary: Arvind Greenfields on Ajwa Road sold 323 units worth INR178 crore, about 42% of launched inventory, in its launch quarter.

segments.name: Mumbai MMR
segments.commentary: Three projects in portfolio: Santacruz redevelopment, Goregaon MHADA redevelopment (JV with Oxford Sigma, 44% profit share), and Pen-Khopoli plotted project (INR1,500 crore, phase 1 INR500-600 crore). Newly signed high-rise worth about INR2,400 crore after year-end.

segments.name: Ahmedabad
segments.commentary: Vastrapur high-rise added in FY26; first launch expected in H1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 BD lock-in target of INR4,000-5,000 crore GDV; BD spend expected slightly above FY26's roughly INR600 crore.
FY27 bookings growth guided at 35-40%, with sustenance sales growing about 15%; long-term bookings CAGR 25-30% over 4-5 years.
About 6 launches planned in FY27 (1 Ahmedabad, 3 Bengaluru, 2 Mumbai) with inventory of INR3,000-3,500 crore; H2 launch weighting expected.
Operating cash flow in FY27 expected to be roughly flat versus FY26 in absolute terms as construction spend ramps.
No explicit revenue guidance; management expects strong growth over FY26 reported revenue as delayed occupation certificates move into FY27.
Projects targeted at 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales; OCF as a share of collections likely 25-30% for next few years.
Net debt-to-equity to stay below 1:1; currently 0.26. Unrealised operating cash flow of over INR4,970 crore expected over 4-5 years.
Final dividend recommended at INR2.25 per share (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: About 6 launches planned in FY27 across Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Mumbai, with some large launches to be phased.
Pen-Khopoli (Mumbai, plotted) is the most advanced Mumbai launch; Santacruz or Goregaon to follow in FY27.
Forest Trails (Bengaluru row houses/villas) site experience and show villa expected ready in 3-4 months; sales activation to restart in FY27.
HDFC platform of INR600 crore, of which INR350 crore used; the balance is being backfilled as available-on-call lines for any product type.
Three HDFC-linked Bengaluru projects use OCD structures.
demand_pricing: Management says demand has stabilised and become more organised after a euphoric period; Bannerghatta's 50%+ sale was a single weekend, with approvals only in the last 7 days of the quarter.
Sustenance sales exceeded INR600 crore in FY26, with about INR180 crore in Q4.
Commodity and material costs up about 4% pre-war versus post-war; management says contingency budgeting absorbs it and no price pass-through is needed yet.
Surat project dropped due to technical and legal complexities.
Cancellations in Forest Trails: about INR11 crore and 5 units in FY26, which management says are part of regular sustaining-stage business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity investment behind FY26 BD and the FY27 BD guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 BD was about INR3,200 crore with investing outflow of about INR600 crore; FY27 BD lock-in target is INR4,000-5,000 crore. Project-wise capital breakup not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the OCF as a percentage of collections stay at 36-37%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to converge to the 22-25% EBITDA margin profile over time; for the next few years it could be 25-30%, helped by plotted projects and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% conservative given launch timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch pipeline is weighted to H2, with the Ahmedabad project possibly in H1; approval slippage is a risk, but management is reasonably sure of timelines.

qa_highlights.question: How will the unsold launched inventory of about INR3,000 crore be sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that about 3 years is a fair assumption for launched inventory, while overall portfolio monetisation is 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be held given rising costs from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 22-25% margins on new sales; a short commodity spike of a quarter or so can be absorbed within budgeted contingency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goregaon JV structure?
qa_highlights.answer: JV with Oxford Sigma on a MHADA redevelopment; Arvind has a 44% profit share, and the partner handles site management and approvals, with Arvind leading development, sales and construction.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition depends on occupation certificates; FY27 revenue recovery depends on timely approvals.
Launch slippage risk: H2 weighting of six launches could push part of the 35-40% bookings growth into FY28.
Commodity cost inflation (about 4% so far) could pressure margins if it lasts beyond a few quarters.
Forest Trails has over 50% unsold inventory and cancellations in FY26.
Sustenance sales growth guided at about 15% in FY27; a slowdown would weigh on bookings.
Shift to OCF-light, asset-light MMR deals and rising construction spend could lower OCF conversion.
539301|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, pipeline and margins, with clear caveats on revenue timing and approvals. Management declined to give revenue or debt guidance and deferred several project-level questions offline.
key_quotes: During the year, we achieved our highest ever annual booking value of INR1,550 crores, representing a strong 22% year-on-year growth.
we are fairly confident that we can continue to maintain the trajectory of 22% to 25% even in the current year.
Having said this, in our own budgeting, we have taken a sufficiently large cushion in the form of contingency and inflation that we normally budget as a part of our practice.
We are at 0.26 net debt-to-equity ratio, as you see.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Net debt-to-equity held below 1:1
rows.why: Net debt-to-equity is 0.26 against a 1:1 cap management says it will not exceed, but BD spend rising to INR4,000-5,000 crore GDV could push debt up.

rows.why: Management expects OCF at 25-30% of collections for the next few years as the mix shifts to plotted and OCF-light MMR deals, against FY26's 36-37% and roughly flat FY27 OCF guidance.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.
539301|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR432 crores grew 147% YoY, with management attributing it to both Aqua City demand and broader core-market strength. Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. Collections grew 76% to INR336 crores and net operating cash flow was INR81 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 35-40% bookings growth, INR4,000-5,000 crores BD and 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales, and India Ratings upgraded the company to AA- (stable).

segments.name: Ahmedabad (Aqua City, horizontal)
segments.commentary: Aqua City named as standout booking performer in Q1; new Vastrapur project planned for launch this year. Management cites leadership in horizontal development in Ahmedabad.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Orchards Phase 1 BU received, driving the quarter's revenue and profit step-up; Bengaluru stock close to INR3,000 crores. Three launches planned this year, including Sarjapur, which has approvals.

segments.name: Mumbai / MMR
segments.commentary: Mumbai stock of INR4,000 crores-plus GDV; two Goregaon redevelopment-related and BD additions. Goregaon saleable carpet area about 6.7 lakh sq ft, 35-floor-plus, about 4 years to complete; 2 Mumbai launches planned this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% over FY26, implying about INR2,100-2,200 crores (per Q&A).
FY27 business development of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV; INR2,600 crores already added in Q1; management leaning to upper band.
EBITDA margin on new sales of 22-25%; management says portfolio average about 25%, JD projects at lower end and outright at higher end.
FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores (FY26 about INR400 crores).
Launch pipeline of about INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects (Ahmedabad 1, Bengaluru 3, Mumbai 2) this year.
Land outflow for FY27 of about INR600-900 crores (Q&A), with 4-5 year realisation of INR5,100 crores operating cash flow from existing portfolio.
Management did not give revenue guidance; expects strong YoY growth in FY27 revenue but timing depends on OC receipts, some lined up in Q4.
Medium-term 25-30% CAGR target over 4-5 years; comfort debt-to-equity at 1:1.
capex_capacity: Unrecognised revenue of INR3,825 crores to be recognised over about 4 years: plotted projects 2-3 years, high-rise OC in about 4 years.
Existing portfolio operating cash flow of over INR5,100 crores expected over next 4-5 years.
Construction spend ramped up in Q1; management says larger incremental outflow is construction cost.
Goregaon redevelopment: 200-plus units to be handed to existing members; area for members not yet disclosed.
Pen Khopoli project in Mumbai awaiting approvals; company hopes to launch at least 2 of 3 Mumbai projects this year.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.
Sustenance sales improved through sales team build-out across 3 cities, channel partner and marketing reach; sustenance may exceed plan.
Price increases expected to moderate after 3-4 years of strong appreciation; company does not underwrite large price hikes.
Bengaluru price uplift giving better margins on some older projects.
Management sees Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad each delivering 22-25% EBITDA; no Tier 2 plans for now.
Management sees annual residential absorption of INR3-4 lakh crores across the three focus markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqua City-driven booking strength project-specific or indicative of underlying demand in Gujarat and Bengaluru?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination of both; the market is strong and stable and responding well to most projects, and underlying demand remains quite strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin was boosted by Orchards BU; the 25% portfolio average is the base case. Revenue recognition is OC-linked and lumpy, so no annual revenue guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 OCF was about INR400 crores; FY27 target INR400-500 crores. Q1 OCF of INR81 crores reflects higher construction outflow, which management views as positive catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity at 0.29x; management comfortable up to 1:1 and expects gradual debt increase, funded by OCF and debt lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores from operating cash flow plus debt headroom; BD cash deployment guided at INR600-1,000 crores in the year (land outflow INR600-900 crores per earlier answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Not today; management is considering it after a few years, starting with for-sale assets to test development before holding assets.

risks_watch: Revenue and margin are lumpy and dependent on OC timing, with some OCs lined up in Q4; the Q1 margin of about 48-49% is well above the 25% portfolio average.
Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.
Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.
key_quotes: Otherwise, our numbers would have been much better in order backlog.
Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% incl. other income, up 0.25-0.3 pts from 12.3% in FY26, helped by O&M and EPC mix, with MDO margin (about 15%) expected to rise about 1 pt a year toward 20-21% at peak capacity.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Tasra washery done Dec 2026; washed coal from Q4 FY27; Tasra
rows.why: KBP mine already producing since Nov 2025 (FY26 offtake ~1.6 Mt vs target ~5 Mt by FY30) and Tasra washery (INR 400 cr capex) is under construction, with ~4 Mt targeted by FY29; ramp is conditional on client offtake and CCL washery readiness.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21% on FY26 revenue of INR 6,107 cr, with MDO revenue targeted at INR 500 cr in FY27 vs INR 226 cr in Q4 FY26 alone (of which INR 117 cr in March), though the FY27 MDO target looks stretched.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only committed capex is INR 400 cr at Power Mech (washery) plus INR 400 cr at Tasra SPV, both debt-free; no utilisation figure is given, and no new plant or line has been announced, so a fresh capex round is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 order inflow missed the INR 10,000 cr target by about 28% (INR 7,210 cr), and FY27 order target of INR 12,000 cr depends on one more BOP win and re-tender of the cancelled INR 1,563 cr West Bengal BESS order.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: MDO FY28 target was already cut from INR 1,800-1,900 cr to INR 1,250 cr, FY27 MDO target of INR 500 cr is well above the Q4 run-rate ex-March, water division has ~INR 900 cr stalled with INR 128 cr awaiting certification, and FY26 orders missed by ~28%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; the only new business lines are MDO ramp-ups already in motion.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow target INR 12,000 cr
rows.why: FY26 inflow was ~INR 7,210 cr (72% of target); FY27 needs BOP wins (~INR 15,000 cr BOP opportunities in 2-3 bids, target one more win), plus Bangalore Metro/Monorail (~INR 10,000 cr, L1 in April) and possible West Bengal re-tender.

rows.label: Water division stall
rows.why: About INR 900 cr contract value stalled pending central/state fund release, INR 128 cr awaiting certification and INR 90 cr receivable; management has stopped new water bids, so this drag persists.

rows.label: BHEL package pricing
rows.why: Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages and BHEL is changing its packaging approach; the 800 MW Singareni BOP (~INR 2,550 cr) and NMDC EPC (INR 8,000-10,000 cr with Thyssenkrupp) hinge on this.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 21% revenue growth, 12.5% margin and long-term power/O&M demand, but cautious on order inflow, water division and MDO timing; analysts pressed on the order miss, MDO FY28 cut and margin path, and some segment figures were revised during the call.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a normal rate of 22-25% should be used, with deferred tax rising next year as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar are capitalised; the Q4 deferred tax charge of about Rs 4-4.5 crore related to land recognised as right-of-use assets for the Madhya Bharat project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

risks_watch: Raw-material cost and supply: ammonia and sulphur prices have roughly tripled and remain volatile; management could not predict when they will ease.
Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.
Q1 FY27 inventory-liquidation benefit is unquantified, and management declined to give numbers; also the Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap is unexplained on the call.
Deferred tax and effective tax rate will rise in FY27 as projects capitalise; a term loan may be used for the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat capex.
Governance and disclosure: management relied on the CFO for most figures and its tone on the call was unusually unstructured.
539334|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid but cautious, emphasising conservatism and a wait-and-see stance on Units 5 and 6 and on FY27 pricing. Its visibility was often hedged ("I can't read too far"), and it repeatedly deferred detailed numbers to the CFO or to later IR follow-up.
key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.
Old numbers will never be seen again.
So we will definitely do Rs. 250 crores in that. Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 250 crores.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable and guides Q1 FY27 PAT at 8-8.5% of revenue versus Q4 FY26 PAT margin of 5.8% and FY26 at 7.1%, but sulphur may settle at Rs 70-75/kg versus Rs 30-35/kg earlier and ammonia has risen from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg, so the gain depends on pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Rabi FY27 (after Kharif FY27, roughly H2 FY27)
rows.why: Unit 6 is about 90-95% complete and Unit 5/6 are mechanically ready, but no Kharif FY27 revenue is assumed from them and commissioning is still unscheduled, with trial production only under evaluation and possibly starting within about one month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 chemical volumes rose 27.9% to 72,423 MT and fertiliser sales were 252,777 MT, but FY27 revenue visibility was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore, with existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore assumed from Rabi season.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 65-70%, so there is no capacity-driven case for new capex, but the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat (Unit 3) plan is already on the table and management said it is still looking for a better opportunity and right time to start it, so timing is undated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from Rs 1,500 crore and management has not factored in higher current selling prices, so an upgrade would need a clear recovery in dispatches that the call does not show.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue has already been cut once (Rs 1,500 crore to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore), demand is weakening as prices rise, Q4 revenue was flat YoY on chemical volume up 36%, and Unit 5/6 timing is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: after Unit 5/6 commissioning, Rabi FY27 onward
rows.why: Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 chemical plants are mechanically ready but no product launch timing or product names were given on the call.

rows.label: Q1 FY27 inventory liquidation
rows.why: Management said held-back Q4 inventory will be liquidated in Q1 FY27 and guided Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore versus Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 218.2 crore, though it declined to quantify the benefit.

rows.label: NBS subsidy adequacy for fertilisers
rows.why: NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but management says it is still insufficient for current raw-material costs, and a 10% government cap is in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 FY27 PAT margin of 8-8.5% and on Unit 6 being 90-95% complete, but cautious on Units 5/6 start-up, FY27 pricing and the Rs 350 crore Unit 3 project, deferring numbers to the CFO and IR; analysts probed the unexplained Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap and capex funding.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

key_quotes: I believe this year will be much better than the last two or three financial years for the company.
So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.
No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5 %- 9%. I hope so.
Honestly speaking, after these sulfur rates came, we put our acid plants on low load.
First, you need value, then volume.
539334|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on FY27 outlook and pricing, repeatedly calling the year much better than the last two or three. It was evasive on volume recovery and on the Q4-to-Q1 order-slippage question, answering by pointing to revenue and profit growth instead. It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

rows.why: EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2% in Q1 with gross margin 31.9%; FY27 PAT guided at 8.5-9% (held), with K-acid price up from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus, but sulphur at about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 is a cost headwind.

rows.why: Cumulative capex Rs 209 crore of Rs 512 crore spent by 30 June 2026; Unit 6 trials expected end-Aug/Sept giving 4-5 months of FY27 operation, adding to 450,000 MT/yr fertiliser and 72,000 MT/yr chemical capacity across Units 5, 6 and Meghnagar.

rows.why: Madhya Bharat project already underway (Rs 60 crore invested to June, 2028 timeline, about twice Unit 6 capacity), Rs 9.3 crore land bought at Lote Parshuram and Rs 125 crore in deposits; utilisation is not disclosed, but acid plants are on low load, so new capacity is not constrained by utilisation.

rows.why: Guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, Q1 chemical volumes fell 39% to 9,113 MT and fertiliser volumes fell 13% to 66,527 MT, and Unit 6 start-up depends on raw material contracts with sulphur at about USD 1,100/t.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said battery-grade phosphoric acid is not on the agenda and the focus is on stabilising current expansions first; the dyes plant (about Rs 37 crore) is already complete, so no new product launch was flagged.

rows.label: K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone inquiries from China
rows.why: Management says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China, while K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus, but no order value was given.

rows.why: Sulphur requires advance payment at about USD 1,100/t versus USD 250-300 earlier, chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1, and Rs 303 crore of the Rs 512 crore capex is still to be spent, so working-capital strain is likely to persist until acid plants restart.

rows.label: Value-over-volume pricing stance
rows.why: Dispatches were stopped in mid-March 2026 to wait for higher prices, fertiliser inventory is being held, and Q1 revenue rose 10% YoY on volumes down 13% (fertiliser) and 39% (chemicals), so realisations are carrying the top line.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 turnover (Rs 1,250 crore, stretching to Rs 1,350-1,400 crore) and pricing, and cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up and on volume recovery; analysts pushed on the Q4-to-Q1 order slippage, the falling acid-plant load, and guidance that moved between figures.

539334|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 58.2% YoY to INR403.5 crore and EBITDA 87.7% to INR49.2 crore, helped by China-driven dye intermediate demand.
539334|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR403.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 58.2% YoY and 44% QoQ, with H1 at INR683.6 crore (+34.1%). EBITDA rose to INR49.2 crore at a 12.2% margin and PAT to INR35.7 crore at an 8.9% margin. Management attributed the gain to China-driven shortages of dye intermediates, Kharif-season volumes and better realisations, and commissioned Unit 5 (about 6,000 TPA dye capacity) and a 10 MW DC solar plant. The board also approved a INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5 (3,000 TPA, commissioning by March 2028) funded partly by a promoter warrant issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR245 crore (+85% YoY), H1 INR383 crore (+53%). Volume 14,368 MT in Q2 vs about 9,000 MT in Q1; margins lifted by Chinese dye intermediate shortages (H-Acid, vinyl sulfone price spikes).

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR158 crore (+27% YoY), H1 INR300 crore (+15%). Q2 volume about 79,000-80,000 MT; H1 about 1,45,000 MT, roughly 1-1.5% below H1 FY26 per management. Management expects Q3 to be subdued.

guidance_outlook: Management sees FY27 revenue of at least INR1,250 crore and says profitability should be in three digits (INR crore); it calls INR1,250-1,300 crore conservative.
FY28 revenue guided at about INR2,000 crore, with a 10% variation (management also cited INR1,800 crore after 10% depreciation).
Management sees scope for EBITDA and PAT margins to improve 15-20% from current levels over time, but said this is not a FY27 target.
Unit 6 trial production expected around end-Nov/Dec 2026; management is assuming no Unit 6 revenue in Q4 FY27 and full production in FY28.
Q3 FY27 chemical volumes expected to be better than Q2; Q3 fertiliser expected to be subdued due to poor season and pending subsidy announcement.
Long-term: management views current footprint as capable of 2.5-3x today's revenue once all capex completes (personal view, not guidance).
Promoter warrant balance (8,54,060 warrants at INR526.90, about INR45 crore) expected by March 2027, ahead of the June 2027 deadline.
capex_capacity: Unit 5 commercial production commenced in Q2 FY27, adding about 6,000 MT per annum of dye capacity; CFO said Unit 5 adds about 1,500 MT per quarter.
Unit 6 is mechanically complete; raw materials being imported; trial production targeted end-November or December 2026, with 3-3.5 months needed for stabilisation, approvals and NBS subsidy claim.
10 MW DC solar at Nanded commissioned; total consolidated solar capacity 20.6 MW DC.
Madhya Bharat Phosphates (wholly owned, Meghnagar, Jhabua, MP) expansion progressing; INR92 crore invested to 30 Sep 2026, funded entirely by internal accruals.

Board approved INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5, Lote Parshuram: 3,000 MT per annum, commissioning by March 2028. Management estimates about INR250 crore revenue at 75% utilisation but declined to name the product.
Withdrawal of the proposed merger of Kisan and Madhya Bharat from NCLT; management said delays made it unviable.
demand_pricing: Chemical pricing firm on China dye intermediate supply gaps from environmental and safety compliance; management called H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price spikes non-sustainable and said they would normalise over weeks or months.
Management said there was no inventory gain from H-Acid, and sulfur prices are starting to ease.
Fertiliser demand supported by availability in drought-affected Maharashtra and MP; about 79,000 MT sold in Q2 despite poor rains. Central subsidy rate not yet declared (expected around 5 November).
Acid complex still running at lower levels because sulfur was high-priced and sulfuric acid could not be sold profitably.
Customer demand recovering gradually after earlier wait-and-watch; management said global demand is still somewhat weak.
Management said receivables were reviewed and are fine; realisations have risen (e.g., INR100 product now selling at INR103-110).

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 to Q2 growth between volume and realisation, and impact of global conflict.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain was a mix of volume (Kharif peak) and realisation, with margins helped by Chinese dye intermediate shortages; Q3 fertiliser to be subdued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 chemical sales (INR245 crore) was opportunistic from H-Acid, and what are margin prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price hikes are not a major driver and are not sustainable; it sees EBITDA and PAT margins better than current levels over time, but declined to quantify FY27 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoter warrant money come in, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance warrant money expected before March 2027, against a June 2027 deadline, to fund Madhya Bharat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall and was there an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin fell from 32% in Q1 to 30% in Q2 (33% in Q2 FY26), attributed to inventory level changes; management denied any inventory gain.

qa_highlights.question: Next-year revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 revenue should be near INR2,000 crore, with about 10% variation, while FY27 is at least INR1,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Kisan-Madhya Bharat merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: NCLT delays made the merger overtaken by events, so management withdrew the application as a conscious decision.

risks_watch: Chemical margins rest on temporary China-driven price spikes in H-Acid and vinyl sulfone; management itself expects normalisation.
Fertiliser H2 subdued by poor monsoon, El Nino and a pending central subsidy rate; Q3 expected weaker.
Unit 6 revenue timing uncertain: trial in Dec 2026, stabilisation and NBS/PDIL approvals may push revenue into FY28.
Management declined to disclose the product or economics of the INR70 crore Unit 5 project, and the capex-per-tonne versus Unit 5's INR37 crore raised questions.
Receivables rising and gross margin dipping QoQ were questioned; the CFO's explanation was limited.
Promoter warrant funding of about INR45 crore is pending shareholder and other approvals and is due by June 2027.
Monitor Q3 FY27 chemical volumes (management expects above 14,368 MT) and the FY27 INR1,250 crore run-rate.
539334|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the headline numbers and FY28 ambition, but guarded and deflecting on H-Acid pricing sustainability, product details of new capex, gross margin drivers and Unit 6 timing. Management repeatedly stressed being conservative while also voicing aggressive long-term targets.

Sir, if I talk about next year, like 2027-2028, in my opinion, we should be somewhere closer to near around INR2,000 crores.
Sulfur is starting to come down, and there was no inventory gain, sir.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The INR1,334.61 crore trading EBIT includes one-offs, so the recurring run rate may be lower (about INR1,000-1,100 crore per management); also watch intersegment transfer pricing, which shifts profit between trading and CGD.
The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.

Cash and other financial assets are unclear: management cited about INR5,000 crore cash, while the balance sheet shows about INR1,300 crore cash plus about INR5,500 crore other financial assets, including GSFS-placed funds. The company will provide a breakup.
Watch Q1 FY27 results (early August 2026) for the first post-merger quarter and EBITDA by segment.
539336|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the merger, the Morbi volume ramp and the long-term sourcing position. Evasive or vague on the power business economics, the cash deployment plan, the transfer-pricing treatment and the balance-sheet cash breakdown, which it deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: We are in the business of making profits, so we cannot be making losses.
The new name reflects the positioning of Gujarat Energy Limited as a true integrated energy Company.
So the price for May was fixed, the price for June is also fixed.
Basically, we have appointed McKinsey. We are working on that.

rows.why: CGD margin guided at INR5.5-6.5/SCM versus about INR6.16/SCM in FY26 (ex-amalgamation), so the range is flat-to-slightly-lower at midpoint; trading margins guided at 4-6% and intersegment transfer pricing is to be optimised.

rows.why: Only CGD capex of about INR1,000 crore (network/station expansion) and E&P drilling of about INR100 crore are guided for FY27, with no named new capacity units or dates; Morbi demand is ramping from 1.66 to about 8 mmscmd and the propane jetty/storage near Morbi is only under discussion.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Morbi offtake has jumped to about 8 mmscmd (710 units) and management is exploring a dedicated propane jetty, JT and storage, but no approvals or dates are given, and the McKinsey-led deployment plan is due next quarter or later.
