tone.note: Management was confident on the merger, Morbi ramp (710 units, about 8 mmscmd) and long-term LNG sourcing, but evasive on power economics (PLF about 1-6.5%), cash deployment, transfer pricing and the cash breakdown, while analysts pressed on spot LNG spreads and the recurring trading run-rate.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.
Management said spot prices near $20/mmBtu make gas costlier than propane, so volume recovery is unlikely near term.
Gas trading sourcing: about 20% long-term (Brent-linked, of which about 20% Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic, about 67% spot.
Gas trading margin: fertilizer marketing margin is fixed at about INR20/scm; industrial margins are market-driven. Management said there will be no negative trading quarters.
Morbi volume rose from about 0.4 mmscmd in April 2026 to about 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the Morbi cluster up 181% vs Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

risks_watch: Morbi volume sustainability: run-rate about 3 mmscmd versus 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts and propane supply recovering.

Gas trading margin durability: Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores against FY27 guidance of about INR1,100 crores, with management stating it is conservative; Q2 visibility limited by Middle East volatility.
CGD EBITDA below guidance at INR5.18/scm against the INR5.5-6.5/scm range; management kept guidance but gave no segment-level explanation.
Third-party gas trading volumes down to about 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, with recovery expected only in FY28-29.

539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.
539400|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was Rs 110 crore, down 25% QoQ, driven by weaker international sales and West Asia disruption. EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ and the highest Q1 domestic revenue to date; brand recall and the SMILE reseller programme (over 1,000 resellers) cited as drivers.

segments.name: International / Export
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.name: Sanand plant
segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

guidance_outlook: Management will not revise the Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28, calling it a stretch but still a goal.
Top-line guidance of about 10-12% growth maintained; management hopes to reach the Rs 600 crore level for the year.
Export and domestic mix expected to approach 50:50 by year end, which management called realistic.
Aim to return to the regular margin profile, helped by price pass-through and Sanand efficiency.
Europe expected to grow YoY this year, with a target to recover the lost sales over the next three quarters; the India-EU FTA effect is seen mainly from next year.

New FR workwear (EN/US certified) launched for own brand and white label; value-added products cited at about 60-70% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Are raw material prices trending and how should margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked products remain at escalated levels versus pre-war; overall RM costs are higher than at start of calendar year, with some easing. Pass-through is gradual because of long-term fixed-price contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much export growth was lost and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin base now and what about under-recovery and FX?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a base and the aim is to grow from here. CFO said there is no under-recovery after the price increases taken at the start of the quarter, and no FX gain as costs are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not revise the target now, calling it a stretch, and levers include capacity, distribution, new geographies, FTAs and larger contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Sanand revenue target and new lines?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Have any large LATAM or US export contracts been won?
qa_highlights.answer: Some long-term contracts exist for workwear and footwear. Large new contracts are not expected quickly; US demand is uncertain due to tariffs.

risks_watch: Export demand in Europe and LATAM remains weak; Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1.
White-label price pass-through lags, so margin recovery depends on contract renewals within the year.
US tariff uncertainty and importer hesitation; no large US contract yet.
Port congestion and container availability disrupting shipments and Middle East supply.
Revenue must rise to earn back the fixed-cost absorption lost in Q1 (lower turnover).

539404|2026-03.headline: Satin Creditcare FY26 consolidated PAT rose 79% to INR330 crores; Q4 PAT up 125% QoQ, with FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20%.
539404|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated AUM of INR15,174 crores (up 19% YoY), revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 23%) and PPOP of INR928 crores (up 23%). Consolidated PAT was INR330 crores for FY26, and Q4 PAT rose 640% YoY and 125% QoQ, which management attributed to lower credit costs and growth, not one-offs. Standalone GNPA was 3.1% at March 2026 and credit cost fell to 3.8% for FY26 from 4.6% in FY25, with Q4 at 2.5% standalone and 2.2% consolidated. Management guided FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% and credit cost of 3-3.5%, and raised its 2030 consolidated AUM target to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores.

financial_highlights.value: FY26 3.8% standalone; 3.55% consolidated; Q4 2.5% standalone, 2.2% consolidated (INR79 crores)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 standalone -77 bps vs 4.6% in FY25

segments.name: Standalone microfinance (JLG)
segments.commentary: Standalone AUM INR12,853 crores (+14% YoY) with disbursements of INR11,202 crores; UP is 23% of portfolio with PAR 90 of 3%, Assam PAR 90 0.7%, Punjab 1.5%. Stage 3 coverage 73% (from 67% in Dec 2025); on-book provisions INR273 crores (2.9%) vs RBI requirement INR172 crores.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,267 crores, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA about 3%, CRAR 53.8%; ICRA A- stable. Average yield about 15.5-16%.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL, MSME subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,054 crores, up 92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; 121 branches in 14 states; disbursed INR255 crores across 34 green loans. Lending is secured by receivables, equipment and property, per management.

segments.name: Satin Technologies (STL)
segments.commentary: Enterprise tech (HRMS, LMS, core banking, cybersecurity, agentic AI); first two clients within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives (SGAL)
segments.commentary: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF, a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs; MOU with SBI for co-investment; progressing toward first close with soft commitments.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone AUM growth 15-20% YoY, implying about INR14,800-15,100 crores.
FY27 standalone credit cost target 3-3.5% vs 3.8% in FY26.
Consolidated AUM growth management estimate about 25-30% (average), so consolidated AUM roughly doubles toward the 2030 target.

Standalone net worth (INR3,129 crores) exceeds consolidated (INR2,868 crores) due to an old revaluation gain, which has limited analytical value.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SFL serves graduated MFI customers and green-finance/micro-enterprise borrowers, underwrites on cash flows and internal scores with data analytics, and lends on secured terms (receivables, equipment, property). It did not give a percentage of the book secured by property; LTV is about 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for April X-bucket collection efficiency and whether geopolitical issues are causing stress.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April is holding at a similar level to Q4 (99.9%) but did not give a figure, and said there is no stress from the geopolitical situation in any state. Q4 overall collection efficiency was a little over 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether there was any one-off in Q4 PAT, including forex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off; Aditi Singh attributed the Q4 PAT rise to reduced credit cost and the growth strategy. Management did not separately quantify the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 ROA guidance and whether ROA above 3% is achievable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give explicit ROA guidance, saying it is a function of AUM growth and credit cost; it said it expects ROA to be better than FY26's 2.6% and that the direction is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the consolidated AUM path to the 2030 target and the growth pace.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15-20% guidance applies to standalone MFI only; consolidated growth is expected to average about 25-30%, which supports the revised INR32,000 crore 2030 AUM target (from INR25,000 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR144 crore net gain on derecognition of financial instruments and whether treasury income is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated INR144 crore line includes a INR92 crore FX effect offset by a corresponding finance-cost item, while derecognition gains are DA income and fair-value gains are treasury income on mutual funds and forex contracts. Management said treasury income is incidental to liquidity, and that NIM is broadly stable at 13.5-14% over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the RBI yield-cap risk and whether the MFI yield of about 25% is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator's interest-rate focus should be read in the context of financial inclusion, doorstep delivery, elevated credit cost and cost of funds, and risk-based pricing. It did not say how it sees future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut.

539404|2026-06.headline: Satin Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 182% YoY to INR120 crore after absorbing a INR36 crore management overlay; reported ROA 3.55%.
539404|2026-06.overview: Satin reported its 20th consecutive profitable quarter and its strongest Q1 in eight years, with consolidated AUM of INR15,935 crore (up 27% YoY, 5% QoQ) and record Q1 disbursements. Standalone NIM rose to 14.36% from 13.16% and cost-to-income improved to 44.49%. Management chose to absorb a INR36 crore management overlay, which lowered reported ROA to 3.55% (4.34% adjusted) and ROE to 15.10% (18.46% adjusted). Guidance for FY27 was kept at 20-25% consolidated AUM growth, 3-3.5% credit cost and 3.5-4% reported ROA, with a review at the half year.

financial_highlights.change: from 13.16% YoY; DA income INR94 crore in Q1 vs ~INR140 crore in Q4

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,360 crore, up 134% YoY and 29% QoQ across 121 branches in 14 states; CRAR 27.1%.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (SHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,263 crore, up 31% YoY; CRAR 59.8% across 57 branches in 22 states.

segments.name: Green finance book
segments.commentary: Reached INR624 crore; INR294 crore disbursed across 50 loans in Q1; ~45% of sustainable and emerging businesses portfolio in clean mobility and renewables.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs
segments.commentary: First paying HRMS customers in Q1; QTrino Labs reached first customer revenue milestone. Core banking platform in customer UAT, go-live targeted Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Progressing toward first close of Category 2 AIF, with first deployment expected in the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated AUM growth of 20-25% in FY27, implying INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027.
Standalone reported credit cost of 3-3.5% for FY27, inclusive of any buffer built.

NIM expected to stay in a 14.35-14.50% steady-state range.
Guidance to be reviewed at the half year depending on monsoon; long-term target INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by 2030 with 30% from non-MFI.
Non-MFI share of consolidated AUM at 19% vs 14% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.
capex_capacity: Added 41 standalone branches in Q1; total 2,041 branches, 34 lakh clients, 3.9 lakh centres, 18,518 employees.
Commenced operations in Kerala in June 2026, adding to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
392 branches added in FY26 are seasoning; operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4.
AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
Breakeven rule of thumb for a new branch: about 1,000 customers, typically reached in about 9 months.
INR100 crore promoter infusion approved by shareholders at about a 17% premium to the minimum issue price, to fund subsidiary growth.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter; management called Q1 disbursements the highest first-quarter disbursements in company history.

Assam floods hit 3 districts (Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo): about 44,000 borrowers and INR149.83 crore outstanding affected, of which INR96.95 crore is covered by nat-cat insurance. Management says Assam ex-those districts is 100% on target.
Bank share of outstanding MFI loans fell to 26.4% from 32.6% a year ago; NBFC-MFI share rose to 43.7% from 38.9%.
Marginal cost of borrowing down 37 bps YoY to 10.52%; 77 active lenders; top 10 lenders are 52% of borrowing; INR2,000 crore direct assignment sanction from a public sector bank.
Undrawn sanctions of INR2,600 crore; INR3,000 crore raised in the quarter including INR285 crore subordinated debt (sub-debt total INR497 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How large should the management overlay buffer be built annually or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not committing to a number; the buffer depends on macro and field conditions and may not be needed. On-book provision is INR250 crore against an RBI requirement of INR152 crore.

qa_highlights.question: DA income trajectory and sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: DA is kept at 20-22% of AUM; Q1 DA was INR94 crore (Q4 was heavier at about INR140 crore). Q2 and Q3 should be in a similar range; Q4 is seasonally heavier.

qa_highlights.question: Gross slippages and write-offs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were INR49 crore (vs INR90 crore in Q4). Write-offs were INR127 crore, elevated because GNPA fell by about 90 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Stress from monsoon or Assam?
qa_highlights.answer: Assam is covered largely by nat-cat insurance; only about 5% of the Assam portfolio (INR149 crore) is affected, of which 3.5-4% is insured, leaving about 1% exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated AUM guidance lower than last quarter's 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says guidance is deliberately conservative; it expects to achieve 20-25% and stable-state growth of 20-25% in FY28 is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is credit cost up while asset quality improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages halved to INR49 crore and GNPA fell 90 bps, but the overlay rose from a little over INR20 crore to INR36 crore, lifting reported credit cost.

risks_watch: Monsoon impact on rural cash flows over the next 2-3 months; Assam collections in the three flood-hit districts.
Negative carry from surplus liquidity: quarter-end drag about 0.15-0.20%, lower over the full quarter per management.
Forex: INR3 crore net negative impact in Q1 from hedged ECB (INR1,573 crore outstanding) accounting mismatch between servicing income and finance cost.
Subsidiary returns remain dilutive during scale-up; consolidated ROA is in an investment phase.
Credit cost guidance of 3-3.5% reported; further overlay additions would depress reported ROA.
key_quotes: We chose not to because we have just come through a cycle in which returns across the sector swung violently and we don't want to be among those who report their best numbers at the top and having nothing left when the turn comes.
So we are not committing a number to it. It will all depend on how the macroeconomics as well as the field level things pan out to be.

But what our idea is, we look at the complete ecosystem and the way how the field operations pan out to be, and that is the reason why we came out with this number and try and look at that and build that kind of a software.
But it's not a guidance. But having said that, we will probably be in the same bracket in the stable zone even in FY28.
Now 15.85% as compared to 14.50% is a slight aberration because the last quarter, as I always said, is probably the most heaviest quarter.
539404|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and franchise durability, but deliberately cautious on returns: management chose to absorb a INR36 crore overlay and repeatedly framed guidance as conservative. 539437|2026-03.headline: IDFC First Q4 FY26 reported PAT of Rs 319 crore after a Rs 646 crore fraud charge; management puts normalised PAT at Rs 746 crore.

Management's normalised PAT is Rs 746 crore, up about 145% YoY, and FY26 PAT adjusted for the fraud was Rs 2,119 crore (up 39%). Loans grew 20% YoY to about Rs 2.9 lakh crore, but customer deposits grew only 1% QoQ, which management attributes to SA rate cuts, the fraud incident, tight liquidity and the West Asia crisis. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 1.61% and credit cost at 1.63% in Q4 versus 2.13% for FY26. Management guided FY27 NIM at about 5.75%, opex growth of 13-14%, and credit cost of 170-180 bps, but would not commit to a 1% ROA timeline.

539448|2026-03.headline: IndiGo posted a Q4 FY26 net loss of 25.4 billion rupees, driven by 48.2 billion rupees of FX losses; FY26 underlying profit ex-FX and exceptionals was 75 billion rupees.

Q4 capacity growth slowed to 3% (about 10% in Jan-Feb) and PRASK fell 4% to 4.46 rupees. Management guided to a mid-teens PRASK increase for Q1 FY27 on fuel charges and a low base, but flagged higher costs and a seasonally softer period from mid-June, with capacity recalibration planned.

539448|2026-06.headline: IndiGo swung to a net loss of INR 2.4 billion in Q1 FY27 as fuel CASK rose ~80% YoY, despite yield growth of 21.3%.

Net loss was INR 2.4 billion against a profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency the loss was about INR 56 million. Yield rose 21.3% and load factor fell 1.3 points to about 83%, but fuel cost rose sharply on Middle East-linked jet fuel prices and the rupee's depreciation of more than 11%. For Q2 FY27 management guided flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25%, while holding the single-digit FY27 ASK guidance.

539450|2026-03.headline: S H Kelkar Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA Rs 83 crore at 13.5% margin, steady sequentially; management guides ~13.5% for H1 FY27 despite raw-material inflation.
539450|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA was Rs 83 crore at a 13.5% margin, flat sequentially, after a one-off sale of about Rs 35 crore of low-margin products. FY26 reported EBITDA margin was 10.2%, with PAT hit by a higher consolidated tax rate from loss-making subsidiaries. Management said raw-material inflation (inventory prices up 12-13%+) had not yet hit Q4 but will show in coming quarters, and it is pricing through to clients on a 2-3 month inventory cycle. FY27 capex is guided at about Rs 140 crore and borrowings at about Rs 800 crore, with a full-year guidance withheld due to uncertainty.

539450|2026-06.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.

Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. Global Ingredients was softer on supply gaps, and Fragrances India was flat as the company exited low-margin business and repriced clients. Net debt rose Rs 65 crore to Rs 852 crore on inventory build and capex, and a Rs 30 crore insurance exceptional item was booked.

segments.name: Fragrances (Europe and international)
segments.commentary: Healthy growth led by Europe and select international markets. Europe plant operational since May; European capex completed. Segment margins are weighed down by higher R&D and global CDC opex.

segments.name: Fragrances India
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, against a strong Q1 FY26 base. Company exited low-margin business and held back shipments until price corrections were agreed; about 95% of clients accepted price increases.

segments.name: Global Ingredients
segments.commentary: Softer quarter on lower demand in select export markets and supply gaps from raw-material constraints; management expects recovery in H2.

Quarterly depreciation about Rs 35 crore, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate capitalisation.
demand_pricing: Price corrections passed to about 95%+ of clients after raw-material cost inflation linked to West Asia geopolitics; clients reluctant to accept were not supplied until negotiations concluded.

Global Ingredients supply curtailed due to raw-material uncertainty; backward integration and China de-risking steps said to be in place.
Unilever and global accounts: ongoing project flow but no large new breakthroughs; Unilever's own pricing pressures and weak India launches noted.

Around 10-11% of revenue comes from products launched in the last 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year Flavours budget and how much did FX add to revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Flavours was Rs 112 crore versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore pulled forward. Like-for-like growth was about 9%, and FX added about 5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is flat India Fragrance a high-base effect, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was strong. The company deliberately exited low-margin business, held back shipments during price negotiations, and says it now services almost all clients after building inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be guided for FY27, and is the Q1 gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise full-year range was given. Management says Q1 is a normal quarter, not exceptional, so EBITDA should be similar in absolute terms if double-digit growth continues, with margin varying about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe ramp-up and return profile?

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance claim status and how is depreciation trending?

539450|2026-09.headline: S H Kelkar H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% to Rs.1,299 crore and EBITDA 33% to Rs.168 crore, with margin at 13%.
539450|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 15% YoY to Rs.636 crore, and H1 revenue reached Rs.1,299 crore (up 14%). H1 EBITDA rose 33% to Rs.168 crore, margin about 13%, with gross margins broadly stable despite raw material volatility. Flavour revenue grew 47% in H1 to Rs.184 crore, though management called part of Q1 a one-off inventory build by customers. Net debt stood at Rs.911 crore at September 30, 2026, which management expects to be the peak for the year as inventory is reduced.

segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.1,088 crore, up 11.9% YoY; management cites about 14% underlying growth excluding roughly Rs.50 crore of low-margin business hived off in Q4 FY26. Domestic growth about 9% (roughly 5% price, 4% volume).

segments.name: Flavour
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.184 crore, up 47% YoY; Q2 revenue about Rs.72 crore versus a Q1 that was higher. Management sees Rs.90 crore per quarter as the run rate and about 20% sustainable growth.

segments.name: Overseas CDCs (Germany, UK, US)
segments.commentary: First sales achieved in all three markets; revenue is small and management says it will take 12-18 months to become meaningful. Around Rs.80 crore of spend in these centres is not yet generating meaningful revenue.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 12-13% per year on a continuing basis over the next 2-3 years, with EBITDA growth of 13-14% per year.
Gross margin expected in the 43% range; upside of about 0.5% if raw material and geopolitical conditions ease.
EBITDA margin of 15%+ targeted within 12-18 months at steady-state inflation, or about two years if inflation persists; 13% described as the lower end of sustainable.
Interest cost expected at Rs.16-17 crore per quarter in H2 FY27; D&A expected at Rs.145-150 crore annualised after new facility capitalisation.
Net debt expected to fall from September 2026 peak by March 2027; insurance claim settlement expected by March 2027.

India Fragrance factory renewal expected to be completed and put to use in Q4 FY27; transition from Mulund follows in FY28.
Second factory (Vanavate or Vashivali) expected to be put to use in Q4 FY28, concluding the large expansion.
Jakarta (Southeast Asia) factory in full operation since September 2025, improving lead times to clients.
Overseas development centres in Germany, Manchester (UK) and US are fully staffed and in use; no further CDC investment planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic Fragrance growth split roughly 5% price and 4% volume; large clients are growing faster than smaller clients, which management calls transient.
Excluding about Rs.25 crore of intentionally exited low-margin categories, like-for-like growth is about 12%.
Management expects a stabilisation in raw material prices and strong H2 demand, but flagged the Middle East situation as the biggest risk.
Flavour growth in Q1 was partly a one-off as customers built inventory due to freight and logistics disruption; management expects about 20% sustainable growth.
More than 5,000 clients served globally; no specific RFQs cited. Europe and US smaller-brand and mid-size opportunities are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fragrance growth split between volume and value in domestic market?

qa_highlights.question: When will inventory unwind and working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory reduction started in October 2026; management does not expect a sharp total inventory fall but expects lower inventory intensity as sales grow over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable interest and depreciation run rate?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Flavour Q2 run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 at about Rs.72 crore was below the normal run rate and Rs.90 crore per quarter is the right run rate; Q1 was above it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE below 12% since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mature India businesses earn about 20% ROCE; overseas investment, the 2024 expansion and fire-related domestic capex weigh on the figure. Rs.80 crore of CDC spend is not yet earning returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone margin low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations moved to subsidiaries KFG and KFL after the fire, so standalone margins are not representative and should recover once operations move back next year.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, raw material inflation and availability, and geopolitical outcomes after the US midterm elections.
Net debt of Rs.911 crore at September 2026 and working capital tied up in high inventory; delivery on the March 2027 reduction target.
Flavour growth lumpiness from customer order timing and inventory destocking after Q1 one-off demand.
Overseas CDCs take 12-18 months to become meaningful; ROCE remains below 12% in the near term.
Execution of Fragrance factory renewal (Q4 FY27) and second factory (Q4 FY28) with capex spillover into FY28.

key_quotes: We expect September debt level to represent a peak for the year with the reduction anticipated by March 2027 as we optimize inventory levels.

539523|2026-03.headline: Alkem Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.6% YoY to INR36,033 million and FY26 EBITDA crossed INR3,000 crore, with management guiding FY27 margins to 20-21%.

Q4 EBITDA was INR5,174 million at a 14.4% margin, and FY26 EBITDA grew 32.2% YoY per management, with a 20.4% full-year margin. Q4 net profit was INR2,365 million after exceptional items of INR602.7 million (labour code gratuity/leave liability) and INR747 million (real estate impairment). Management flagged rising logistics, API and packaging costs from geopolitical disruption, and announced that CEO Dr. Vikas Gupta is leaving; a new CEO search is underway.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for India growth and the margin path given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: India is targeted at 100-150 bps above the market; FY26 margin of 20.4% is the baseline and FY27 is seen at 20-21%, with 100 bps annual expansion now a moving target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech deal timing and the impact on numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Deal expected to close in 45-60 days; if it closes, Q2 FY27 would carry a full quarter impact. Medtech is under 1% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.answer: US approval is possibly by Q1 CY27 subject to inspection; no launch this year. Europe has one partner for the Prolia biosimilar; the Xgeva version has no partner yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan launch and expected contribution?

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
539524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.

International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.

Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.

Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.

Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.

Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.

I think we need the cycle to run through quarters for us to say that it has really caught on because we have not yet entered fever season this time round.

539551|2026-03.headline: Narayana Q4 FY26: India margin rose to 25.1% (from 21.5%), but consolidated EBITDA dipped to ~20% on UK acquisition costs; management gives no formal guidance.

The UK business (PPG, acquired with five months in FY26) diluted consolidated margins and PAT; management says ~200 bps of the ~500 bps margin drop was one-time deal costs, normalising to ~22%. Cayman insurance losses (USD 5 million in the quarter) remain high, with a loss ratio of about 110–112% and price increases from June. India clinics continue to lose cash because of corporate overheads, and FY26 greenfield capex was only INR 109 crore against INR 424 crore planned.

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +56.9% YoY; +16.3% QoQ (Q1 FY26 Rs 464 mn; Q4 FY26 Rs 626 mn)
+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)
+95% YoY (from Rs 60 mn); +39.3% QoQ (from Rs 84 mn)
Management said it improved steadily through FY26

segments.name: Direct advertisers
segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.name: PiiX (Apple ecosystem)
segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

guidance_outlook: Long-term 'Rule of 50' framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% or higher, with a vision to 2030.
Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.
Expects a growing share of optimisation decisions to be made by the Neural Engine over the next 12 to 18 months.
FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Mobavenue Neural Engine launched as a unified AI layer at the core of GMP360; management said core decisioning moved fully to neural network systems in FY26.
Platform processes over 1.3 billion signals per day and reaches about 2.6 billion devices monthly, with decisions in under 15 milliseconds.
Campaign lifecycle (plan, launch, create, report) said to run in under 59 seconds / under a minute per step.
Asset-light model; management said platforms can scale with limited incremental infrastructure investment.
Balance sheet supported by a FY26 preferential raise (about Rs 50 crore per an analyst's reference); capital prioritised for AI stack, international expansion and selective acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Growth led by direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail, plus premium formats such as connected TV and video streaming.
Revenue per outcome of Rs 49.94 on 14.16 million verified outcomes; management said both outcomes and price per outcome are rising.
Top five sectors (FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Travel) contribute about 70-80% of revenue; management did not disclose top-5 or top-10 client shares.
Data and supply costs are the largest cost line and are largely variable with revenue.
Named global competitors: AppLovin, Unity and The Trade Desk; named India competitors: Affle and InMobi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.
Regulatory risk, which management named as the primary risk; also currency risk and AI disruption.
Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.
Deployment of the FY26 preferential raise into acquisitions, which management has not yet named.
539682|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability; the tone was more qualitative when answering questions on client concentration, the scale of PiiX revenue and the acquisition pipeline, where few figures were given.
key_quotes: We do not optimize it for a quarter or 100 days. We optimize for the whole year.
The general market growth cannot do 56.9%. Right.
Our revenue per outcome improved steadily through FY26. Q1 FY27, our platforms delivered 14.16 million verified outcomes at Rs. 49.94 per outcome.
We own all three P3 layers on our proprietary technology infrastructure. Most platforms own one or two and license the rest.
Yes, I think in the listed player, it is Affle, which is one of it. InMobi is another

539686|2026-03.headline: K.P. Energy FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore (up 57% YoY) and Q4 PAT hit a record INR 78.69 crore.
539686|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR 1,505.54 crore (up 57% YoY), EBITDA of INR 328.44 crore (up 68%) and PAT of INR 181.4 crore (up 57%). Q4 net sales reached an all-time quarterly high of INR 631.81 crore, up 83% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 21% (up 194 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 78.69 crore. The order book is about 2 GW (INR 3,000 plus crore), with about 230 MW added in Q4, while operating cash flow weakened due to higher inventory (WTG turbines) and advances. Management guided to 40-50% growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +83% QoQ from INR 344.96 crore in Q3 FY26; all-time quarterly high
+71% YoY; margin 21% vs 19% in Q4 FY25 (+194 bps)
+72% YoY from INR 45.79 crore; highest ever quarterly PAT

segments.name: EPC and infrastructure development
segments.commentary: Core engine at INR 1,451.69 crore in FY26 (+59% YoY). Order book of about 2 GW valued at roughly INR 3,000 crore, about 50% from Group entities.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 5.13 crore (+350% YoY); manages over 646 MW under O&M, supported by a 24x7 NOC using IBM Maximo-based AI alerts and SCADA dashboards.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: Operational portfolio of 48.5 MW at year-end; a further 200 MW of IPP capacity is under development (two 100 MW projects). Q4 IPP revenue declined YoY on marginally lower wind performance, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance of 40-50%, which management said is backed by sufficient orders in hand.
Scale EPC execution to convert the near 2 GW order book into revenue; majority of current order book expected to be completed by FY27.
Long-term target of 10 GW total portfolio by 2030; current renewable portfolio exceeds 3.7 GW and projects in hand exceed 2.1 GW.

Offshore wind and PSP (pumped storage) being evaluated; India's offshore plan is 30 GW by 2030 with initial 4 GW bids off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. Management said the segment is at a nascent stage and it awaits central policy and VGF clarity.

Power sales from IPP were 6.18 (Q3) and 5.62 (Q4), per management, which it said was a nominal change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall sharply versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shabana Belim attributed it to a rise in inventory (WTG turbines) ahead of upcoming projects, amid geopolitical supply risk; debtors were broadly stable relative to revenue growth. Cash conversion cycle ranges from 100 to 150 days depending on customer.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital normalise once the geopolitical situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital will stay higher in proportion to 55% revenue growth plus upcoming order mobilisation; higher inventory will convert into debtors over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 gross margin typically lower and how do turbine-included EPC margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were in line with prior periods and EBITDA margin improved to 21.82% in FY26 from 20.46% in FY25; turbine-inclusive EPC contracts carry a somewhat lower margin than EPC-only contracts because of pre-booked turbine leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IPP unit generation and revenue decline in Q4 YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a marginal decline in wind performance in Q4 and described it as seasonal, with no concern on operating assets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is Group versus non-Group, and when will it be executed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR 3,000 plus crore order book is from Group entities; the pipeline excludes Group entities. Majority of current orders expected to complete by FY27, with more additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CERC trading licence and its revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India's FY25 short-term trading of about 230 BU out of 1,830 BU generated and IEX FY26 volume of 141 BU (up about 17%); no timeline or revenue figure was given.

IPP generation seasonality and wind performance (Q4 IPP revenue down YoY).
